General statement. thm:parity-chain-degree-ceiling and cor:neighborhood-homology-ceiling compile the precise topological certificate. cor:kneser-parity-ceiling applies a fixed local label map to full graphs only. prop:high-girth-homology-witness proves the graph screen is non-vacuous. prop:perfect-binary-moment-rank and prop:disjoint-product-map-degree give all-parameter scope controls; ex:kernel-review-controls records the exact finite checks.

Across the goal

  • Near-half Boolean PC family. Open. All six research entries since the last goal-level review took this obligation as primary and reported it unchanged. They excluded the old noncentral source, repaired it by central targets, built compatible selectors, proved their dimension and full-module limitations, supplied stronger conditional sections, and excluded low-error point supports. None proved a surviving global unit at the target cutoff. The open-item count has not dropped from two since the review twelve research entries back.
  • Complete Frege transfer. Open. Zero research cycles in this block took this obligation as primary. The imported weighted-map tools apply only after an appropriate old pseudoideal and coherent maps exist. Growing logarithmic width still has no complete transfer ledger. The old family remains the highest-risk prerequisite.

Obstacle

The missing implication is global: an actual unbounded unsatisfiable Boolean source must have a proper kernel containing its active axioms and stable under every legal multiplication after cancellation. Local immunity, all-pin affine fullness, compatible scalar sections, an exponentially large ambient space and a static normalized annihilator do not establish it. The prescribed padded-fall test from the previous review was settled by absorption, but did not control the complete defect space or the unit.

Architecture review

Necessary target. For each fixed relevant \(\ell\ge2\), give a polynomial-size Boolean CNF family on actual \(v\to\infty\), independent of the proposed size exponent, with \(1\notin C_D\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), where \(D=\lfloor v/2-s\rfloor\), \(s=o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\). A proper degree-D linear kernel containing the inputs and closed on its degree-at-most-D-minus-one part suffices. Its exponential quotient dimension and some large free coordinate set are necessary consequences, not optional properties. A separate construction of a larger quotient or a prescribed free set is unnecessary.

Extra requirements. Full Boolean coefficient modules and globally commuting operators add uncharged restriction behavior that the goal does not require. The latest conditional sections are raw data with coefficient degrees as large as the row width; they do not provide degree-one transport. All-pin local surjectivity and a separately chosen common moment vector were sufficient conveniences for that construction, not requirements on every hard formula. A single unit-separating functional for the full row-closed span is a weaker necessary intermediate target; it must not be reported as a PC invariant.

Independent alternative. Before seeing the preferred route, the sole medium reviewer received only the goal and bounded statements. It found no justified new lower-bound architecture and proposed the compact four-colour/Kneser route as an exploratory alternative. It correctly retained the degree and variable budgets and later clarified that the dimension floor is necessary. Its proposed quadratic edge representation is already the proved degree-four translation; it is not new progress. The actual queued Kneser witness uses edge-minimal cores, so full-graph results need not survive deletion. The review below tests a genuinely different implication of topology: a parity certificate can make the original colouring formula easy. The independent-stage response is retained.

Rank normalization. Continue to use one quotient, its actual unit and the induced multiplier maps. Exponential dimension is necessary but does not identify the marked class. A symmetric Gram matrix over a perfect binary field cannot replace positivity, and independent parameter choices do not imply independence of kernels in a shared truncated weight space. The auxiliary imports below distinguish fresh coefficient classes from the full old-variable coefficient module excluded here.

Decision. Retain the queued Reed–Muller source for the next direct global test, and first address unit survival in its explicitly defined sum of complete row-ideal pieces. This weakens the next positive deliverable without changing the goal: even a successful static separation leaves multiplication open. Stop refining local conditional ranks as the main task. Keep the colouring alternative, adding the proved homology screen only in its paid compact encoding; high-girth critical graphs witness that the screen is not vacuous. No automatic exclusion of arbitrary Kneser cores is made.

Decisive test. For the original random-half source \(k=\lceil2\log_2v\rceil,m=v+k\), use \(D=\lfloor v/2-v/(\log(v+2))^{\ell-1}\rfloor\) and the full Boolean algebra \(B\). Put \(K_D=\sum_a(J_a\cap B_{\le D})\), where each \(J_a\) is the cylinder vanishing ideal of its actual row. The next cycle must try to construct a functional annihilating this entire space and taking one to one, or an explicit decomposition of one into those degree-D row pieces. The endpoint is high-probability static properness on the original independent source, or at least a proved unbounded choice of unsatisfiable instances with this property; an exclusion must likewise cover an unbounded regime. Finite separation examples do not discharge it. The probability statement concerns the original independent source, not an adaptively selected core.

The existing evaluation duality makes the exact global domain available: if \(E=B_{\le v-D-1}\) and \(U_a\) is the space of functions supported on the allowed cylinder of row \(a\), seek \(w\in\bigcap_a(E+U_a)\) with \(\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^v}w(x)=1\). The identity \(B_{\le D}^{\perp}=E\) under full-cube binary evaluation pairing and the annihilator-of-intersection rule give this description. It is the already known local-design criterion in a Reed–Muller domain, not a new theorem or an assumed solution. A small local coefficient list is not this exponential space. If one enters \(K_D\), the original-width derivations of local relations and final-line multiplication give an actual degree-D PC refutation for large \(v\). If a separator is constructed, report only that global static properness and then test the fixed-cutoff multiplier images. Merely reproducing this duality, a dimension count or a larger local matrix does not answer the test.

A characteristic-two chain compiler

Let \(K\) be a finite simplicial complex with a simplicial involution \(\tau\). Work with unoriented simplicial chains over \(\mathbb F_2\). Suppose, for an integer \(m\ge1\), fixed chains satisfy \[c_j\in C_j(K;\mathbb F_2),\qquad \operatorname{aug}(c_0)=1,\qquad \partial c_j=(1+\tau)c_{j-1}\quad(1\le j\le m).\tag{1}\] Let \(\Gamma\) be a canonical Boolean CNF. For each vertex \(u\) of \(K\), let a label function \(L_u\) take values in \(\{\pm1,\ldots,\pm m\}\), depend on at most \(b\ge1\) old Boolean bits, and satisfy \(L_{\tau u}=-L_u\) for every assignment. Require a local certification property: if the labels at an edge \(uv\) are opposite, then the assignment violates an original clause whose variables lie in the union of the bits read at \(u,v\). Labels and chains are fixed functions of the source, not choices made after evaluating a proof line.

Theorem (parity chain ceiling). These data give an ordinary Nullstellensatz refutation of \(\Gamma\) through degree at most \(b(m+1)\) over every field of characteristic two. No Boolean reduction is treated as a free inference, and no bound on the number of simplices is required for the degree assertion.

The local parity identity. Call a multiset of labels positively alternating if their absolute values are distinct and, when ordered by absolute value, their signs alternate starting positive; define negatively alternating similarly. Write \(A_j^+(\sigma),A_j^-(\sigma)\) for the zero-one indicators on a j-simplex. For a label multiset with no opposite pair, \[\sum_{\rho\text{ facet of }\sigma}A_{j-1}^+(\rho) =A_j^+(\sigma)+A_j^-(\sigma)\pmod2.\tag{2}\] Here is a complete count. If a label repeats, only deletion of one of a unique repeated pair can make absolute values distinct, and those two contributions agree; otherwise all facets are non-alternating. With distinct absolute values, order the signs. At least two adjacent equal-sign breaks cannot be removed by deleting one entry. Exactly one break gives two alternating facets with the same starting sign. With no break, only deletion of the first or last entry gives an alternating facet, and exactly one starts positive. These cases prove (2), including two-vertex simplices.

Local canonical compilation. Represent each indicator in (2) by its unique multilinear polynomial on the union of the queried bits of that simplex. This union has size at most \(b(j+1)\). Its difference polynomial vanishes on every assignment satisfying the original clauses supported in that union, since each edge then has no opposite labels. For each assignment where the difference is nonzero, choose one violated such clause. The full assignment indicator is exactly that clause's falsity indicator multiplied by the literals on the other coordinates. Expanding the difference in full assignment indicators therefore expresses it as an ordinary linear combination of input multiples, each of degree at most \(b(j+1)\). The cofactor and clause use disjoint variables. Thus (2) is a paid local identity, not a semantic inference with uncharged degree.

Chain summation. Let \(B_j\) be the evaluation of \(A_j^++A_j^-\) on \(c_j\). The just-derived local identities and (1) give \[B_j=\langle A_{j-1}^+,\partial c_j\rangle =\langle A_{j-1}^++A_{j-1}^-,c_{j-1}\rangle=B_{j-1}.\tag{3}\] Antipodality makes the middle equality an exact polynomial identity. Every vertex is alternating with exactly one sign, so \(B_0=\operatorname{aug}(c_0)=1\). A simplex of dimension \(m\) would need \(m+1\) distinct absolute labels to be alternating, so \(B_m=0\). Summing (3) gives an ordinary input-multiple identity for one through degree \(b(m+1)\). All indicator polynomials and their sums are multilinear; equality as Boolean functions is therefore equality as these ordinary polynomials. The construction uses only binary coefficients and works in every characteristic-two extension. \(\square\)

The parity mechanism is the chain form of Fan's alternating-simplex argument; Prescott–Su's constructive theorem and proof were read. The new assertion here is its explicit ordinary-degree compilation for locally readable Boolean labels. No complex or positive-real theorem is reduced into the proof field.

A graph homology screen with constant degree

For a finite simple graph \(G\), let \(N(G)\) be its neighborhood complex: its simplices are vertex sets with a common neighbor. Let \(B_0(G)\) have vertices \((v,+),(v,-)\) and simplices \(A^+\cup B^-\) whenever every vertex of \(A\) is adjacent to every vertex of \(B\). Either side may be empty. Looplessness makes the sides disjoint, and swapping signs is an involution.

Corollary (neighborhood homology ceiling). Let \(G\) have at least one edge, and let \(c\ge2\), \(b=\lceil\log_2c\rceil\). If \[\widetilde H_i(N(G);\mathbb F_2)=0\quad(0\le i\le c-2),\tag{4}\] then its compact b-bit canonical c-colouring CNF has an ordinary characteristic-two Nullstellensatz refutation through degree \(b(c+1)\). For fixed \(c\), the proof and the chain-finding linear algebra have polynomial size in the graph's vertex count. In particular, for four colours, simultaneous vanishing of reduced homology in degrees zero, one and two gives degree at most ten.

Shift the neighborhood homology. Let \(U\) be the union of closed stars of all positive vertices of \(B_0(G)\), and let \(V\) be the full negative simplex. Then \(B_0(G)=U\cup V\), and \(U\cap V\) is exactly the negative copy of \(N(G)\). The space \(U\) is acyclic. To see this without an equivariant homotopy theorem, add the positive stars one at a time. Each star is a cone. Its intersection with the preceding union is also a cone, on the newly added positive vertex: if a face can be extended by that vertex and by some previous positive vertex, it can be extended by both, since positive vertices impose only adjacency to its negative side. These intersections are nonempty. Induction with the simplicial chain exact sequence for a union proves acyclicity. The full simplex \(V\) is acyclic as well.

The same exact sequence gives \(\widetilde H_j(B_0(G);\mathbb F_2)\cong\widetilde H_{j-1}(N(G);\mathbb F_2)\) for \(j\ge1\), and \(B_0(G)\) is connected because the intersection is nonempty. Explicitly, split a cycle into its U and V pieces; their common boundary lies in the intersection, giving the connecting map. Acyclicity of U and V gives its inverse and trivial kernel. Thus (4) makes reduced homology of \(B_0(G)\) vanish through degree \(c-1\).

Choose a single positive vertex as \(c_0\). Its antipodal norm is a reduced zero-cycle, so it bounds \(c_1\). Inductively \((1+\tau)c_{j-1}\) is a cycle since \((1+\tau)^2=0\) in characteristic two, and the homology vanishing fills it by \(c_j\) for \(j\le c\). These are fixed chains (1).

Colour labels and cost. Label \((v,+)\) by the colour of \(v\) and \((v,-)\) by its negative. For invalid b-bit codes, define the label to be colour one; the original domain clauses forbid those codes. Each label reads exactly b bits and is antipodal. Opposite labels on an edge either expose an invalid code or assign the same valid colour to adjacent graph vertices, violating a canonical input within those two bit blocks. Apply the chain theorem with \(m=c\). There are at most \(O(|V(G)|^{j+1})\) j-faces for every fixed \(j\le c\), and each local truth table has at most \(2^{b(c+1)}\) entries. Binary boundary solving and the resulting input-multiple identity therefore have polynomial size when c is fixed. \(\square\)

Consequently a near-half-hard compact four-colour family must eventually fail (4): at least one of these three reduced binary homology groups must be nonzero. This is a condition on that explicit encoding. It does not say that nonzero homology supplies hardness or that every topological invariant yields such a chain certificate.

Full Kneser graphs and the core boundary

Corollary (Kneser parity ceiling). For every \(k\ge1\) and \(n\ge2k+3\), the full graph \(KG(n,k)\), compactly encoded with four colours, has a binary ordinary Nullstellensatz refutation through degree \(4k+6\). This does not upper-bound arbitrary edge-minimal non-four-colourable subgraphs.

Proof. It suffices to use the induced \(KG(2k+3,k)\). Put \(r=2k+3\) and take the order complex of nonempty signed subsets \((A,B)\) of \([r]\), with \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), ordered by inclusion in both coordinates. It is the barycentric subdivision of the boundary of the r-dimensional crosspolytope. Its coordinate hemispheres provide chains (1) through dimension \(m=r-1=2k+2\): in dimension j, sum the full flags in the positive hemisphere on the first \(j+1\) coordinates. Interior facets cancel in pairs, leaving the two hemispheres of the equator. The zero-chain is one positive vertex.

Fix a total order on subsets refining cardinality. If \(|A|+|B|\le2k-2\), give the node absolute label \(|A|+|B|\), with sign determined by which of A and B is larger in that order. Otherwise the larger side contains a k-subset; query the colour of its first k elements, give it absolute label \(2k-2+\text{colour}\), and use that side's sign. This spherical variant of Matoušek's fixed-query labeling is antipodal and uses labels through \(2k+2\), reading at most two old bits at each node.

Along a strict comparable pair, two low labels have different magnitudes, and low and high ranges are disjoint. Opposite high labels query equally coloured disjoint k-sets: if \(A\subseteq A'\), \(B\subseteq B'\), then \(A\cap B'=B\cap A'=\varnothing\). They therefore violate an original Kneser edge clause within the four queried bits. The chain compiler gives degree \(2(m+1)=4k+6\). The labeling and hemisphere arguments are stated completely here; no Frege-to-PC simulation is assumed. \(\square\)

For \(n=2k+4\), the original graph has exponentially many vertices in k, so this is logarithmic in its actual bit count. However, the queued witness selects edge-minimal cores. Deleting edges can remove the inputs used to certify complementary labels and change neighborhood homology. The corollary gives no reverse proof transfer to those cores. The independent review's full-graph suggestion therefore does not settle the candidate that was actually recorded.

The graph screen is non-vacuous

Proposition (high girth witness). There are unbounded edge-minimal non-four-colourable graphs of girth tending to infinity whose compact two-bit CNFs satisfy the accepted structural envelope and have \(\widetilde H_1(N(G);\mathbb F_2)\ne0\). They have width four, polynomial canonical length, essential blocks, at least four block occurrences of every bit, full binary affine row hulls, no common Horn polarity and a locally shattered set of half their bits. No positive-linear or near-half PC lower bound is asserted for this graph witness.

Existence with the actual size counted. Use the classical high-girth probabilistic construction, with the following complete parameters. Fix an integer \(g\ge5\), choose a sufficiently large integer M, and sample a graph with edge probability \(p=M^{-1+1/(2g)}\). Expected cycles of lengths three through \(g-1\) are at most \(g\sqrt M\). Markov's inequality bounds the probability of more than \(M/10\) such cycles by \(10g/\sqrt M\). The expected number of independent sets of size \(\lceil M/5\rceil\) is at most \[2^M\exp\left(-p\binom{\lceil M/5\rceil}{2}\right)=o(1).\tag{5}\] Choose a graph with both properties and delete one vertex from each short cycle. At least \(9M/10\) vertices remain, and no independent set has size \(\lceil M/5\rceil\). A four-colouring would have an independent colour class of size at least \(9M/40>\lceil M/5\rceil\) for large M, a contradiction.

Take an edge-minimal non-four-colourable subgraph and remove isolated vertices. Every remaining vertex has degree at least four; otherwise a four-colouring after deleting that vertex would extend. Its girth is at least g. It is nonbipartite, so its actual vertex count N is at least g. Taking \(g\to\infty\) proves unboundedness even if the core is much smaller than M. There are \(v=2N\) actual Boolean bits, four width-four clauses per edge and length \(O(N^2\log(N+1))\), with no auxiliaries.

Nonzero neighborhood homology. In a graph with no four-cycle, two distinct neighborhoods intersect in at most one vertex. Every neighborhood simplex can be collapsed, fixing its vertices, to a star on those vertices. Explicitly choose a centre and pair every subset S of its other vertices of size at least two with \(S\cup\{\text{centre}\}\), in decreasing order of \(|S|\). At removal time S has that unique coface, and no other neighborhood simplex contains S. These elementary collapses therefore work in the entire complex. The result is a graph on N vertices with \[\sum_v(\deg(v)-1)=2|E(G)|-N\] edges. If it has t connected components, its first binary homology has dimension \(2|E(G)|-2N+t\), which is positive since minimum degree is at least four. This proves the required failure of (4).

Other specification properties. Edge minimality is block minimality, and the unequal-colour relation is essential in every one of its four bits. Each bit occurs in at least four edge blocks, so its branching fraction is one. The twelve allowed four-bit tuples have full binary affine hull, since a nonzero binary affine function cannot vanish on twelve of the sixteen points. After any coordinate polarity, full affine hull means that no coordinate is fixed. If the renamed row were meet-closed, intersecting all its allowed tuples would therefore give its all-zero tuple. A common polarity making every row meet-closed would make the global all-zero assignment satisfy every renamed row, contradicting unsatisfiability. Thus no common Horn polarity exists. Selecting one of the two bits at each vertex gives a locally shattered set of size N: whenever the selected bits agree along an edge, choose the two other bits differently. Thus all earlier structural conditions coexist with the new homology screen. \(\square\)

This replaces neither the general guarded width-five witness nor its proved positive-linear degree. It gives a graph-specific non-vacuity control and trades away Kneser containment while strengthening odd-girth control to full girth. Neither witness supplies the near-half conclusion. The necessary graph-specific homology restriction is adopted only in the compact colouring sub-specification.

Two further scope controls

Proposition (perfect binary moment rank). Let F be a perfect field of characteristic two and B a symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional space. If every vector with \(B(u,u)=0\) lies in the radical of B, then \(\operatorname{rank}B\le1\). In particular a nondegenerate anisotropic symmetric form has dimension at most one.

Proof. In a basis, the cross terms in \(B(u,u)\) cancel and perfectness gives \[B(u,u)=\sum_i b_{ii}u_i^2=\left(\sum_i\sqrt{b_{ii}}u_i\right)^2.\tag{6}\] Its zero set is the kernel of one linear form, or the whole space. The radical is always contained in it. The assumed reverse inclusion therefore makes the radical have codimension at most one. \(\square\)

An actual Boolean moment example over \(\mathbb F_2\) is the sum of point masses at \(01,10,11\). On \(1,x,y\) its moment matrix is \[\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}.\tag{7}\] It has rank three, while x has zero self-pairing and nonzero pairing with y. Thus positivity-style inference from zero norm to a radical vector is invalid. This does not prohibit nondegenerate bilinear pairings, which may be useful without anisotropy, and it does not address imperfect transcendental extensions.

Proposition (product map degree). Let \(g=x_A\), \(h=x_B\) be monomials on disjoint nonempty Boolean variable sets of sizes a,b. Over any field, the minimum possible maximum degree of coefficient polynomials \(u,v\) satisfying both complete accuracy-one companion identities \[g(1-ug-vh)=h(1-ug-vh)=0\tag{8}\] as Boolean functions is \(\min(a,b)\). The minimum has Boolean coefficient images, so fresh Boolean equations do not change it.

Proof. The product \(P=1-ug-vh\) equals one where \(g=h=0\), and (8) makes it zero elsewhere. Hence its unique multilinear representative is \((1-g)(1-h)\), of degree \(a+b\). If both maps have degree at most T, reduction cannot raise \(\deg P\le T+\max(a,b)\), so \(T\ge\min(a,b)\). If \(a\le b\), the maps \(u=1,v=1-g\) attain degree a; exchange the roles otherwise. Both maps are Boolean-valued. This is a costed specialization of the historical independent-input barrier, not a new packing principle. \(\square\)

At \(a=b=2\), fixed old weight one and affine coefficient degree \(T=1\), all \(2^{10}\) binary coefficient pairs fail. The complete block has original joint degree five, so this is a legitimate full-window control at \(D\ge5\) in the old Boolean base. The seven affine coefficient equations reduce to the two three-equation prescriptions forcing u and v each to be one at the all-one old point, plus the contradictory requirement that their sum there be one. Their coefficient and augmented ranks are six and seven. Although seven equation degrees are less than ten parameters, zero solutions remain compatible with finite-field divisibility. Degree-two maps give an explicit repair in their larger paid window. The base is satisfiable and the source is easy with that repair; no hard-family obstruction is claimed.

Absurd bridges

  • Quantum error recovery. Knill–Laflamme's recovery criterion controls compressed error products on a complex code space. Translate a marked proof state into a code state and proposed relation errors into correctable operators. Answers. Recovery that also preserved the actual PC kernel under every legal multiplier could answer near-half-pc-family; correctability alone does not identify an error image with zero. Test. Falsified for that identification. On a logical bit tensored with a syndrome bit, let \(P=I_2\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|\) and \(E=I_2\otimes X\). Then \(PEP=0\), \(PE^*EP=P\), and errors in the span of \(I,E\) are exactly recoverable, but \(EP\ne0\) and \(PE^2P=P\). The explicit syndrome recovery is a positive control. These are error operators, not claimed Boolean variable actions; a degree-filtered proof interpretation remains missing.
  • Belief propagation on factor trees. Kschischang–Frey–Loeliger's sum-product rule is exact on cycle-free factor graphs by distributivity, including its semiring formulation. Translate local row states into messages and try to normalize their contraction as a binary witness. Answers. A degree-aware vector-message construction preserving a unit could address near-half-pc-family; exact scalar counting is insufficient. Test. Falsified for automatic normalization: the one-factor tree \(x\ne y\) has messages \((1,1)\) and partition sum two, which is zero over \(\mathbb F_2\). Conditioning \(x=0\) repairs the normalization by selecting the genuine model \(01\), so the failure is not an impossibility theorem for messages. That repair is a satisfiable point witness and does not supply an unsatisfiable truncated invariant; cyclic exactness and degree costs cannot be assumed.

The actual attempted construction

Fix \(\ell\ge2\), \(k=\lceil2\log_2v\rceil\), \(m=v+k\), independent uniform k-coordinate scopes and independent Bernoulli-half allowed tuples. Take \(D=\lfloor v/2-v/(\log(v+2))^{\ell-1}\rfloor\); eventually \(k\le D<v\). Let \(B\) be the binary Boolean function algebra, \(A_a\) the allowed cylinder, \(F_a\) its forbidden complement, and \(J_a\) the ideal of functions vanishing on \(A_a\). The tested space is exactly \[K_D=\sum_a(J_a\cap B_{\le D}).\] The proved source and normalization record supplies unsatisfiability with high probability and actual-variable retention. It supplies no assertion about the displayed sum.

With \(R=v-D-1\), write \(E=B_{\le R}\) and let \(U_a\) be the functions supported on \(A_a\). The review's exact dual seeks \[w\in\bigcap_a(E+U_a),\qquad \sum_xw(x)=1.\tag{1}\] Every summand here is a subspace of the same full Boolean function space. The construction attempt was to choose \(p_a\in E\) with \(w|_{F_a}=p_a|_{F_a}\). On an unsatisfiable instance the \(F_a\) cover the cube. Thus the chosen local restrictions have to agree on every \(F_a\cap F_b\) before they define w. Those agreement equations and the mass equation were not solved.

The simplest proposed completion chooses one common \(p\in E\) for all the \(p_a\). It indeed satisfies agreement but then \(w=p\) on the covering cube, so its mass is zero: every multilinear monomial of degree below v misses a coordinate and sums to zero over the binary cube. This is already the identity \(E=B_{\le D}^{\perp}\), not a new obstruction theorem. Allowing independent local lifts avoids that immediate zero, but their differences must vanish on the forbidden intersections. Local row interpolation alone imposes no solution to these global difference equations. A point-supported repair is already excluded by the proved support bound on an unsatisfiable source at this cutoff.

There is a useful directional check. A theorem saying that every compatible family of these local degree-R restrictions has one global degree-R lift would force all solutions of the homogeneous compatibility equations to have zero mass. In this exact setting it would establish failure of (1), hence an actual unit in \(K_D\), rather than the sought separator. Conversely a failure of that global lifting property is not enough: the resulting class may still have zero mass. This is an application of the existing separation criterion, not progress from renaming the obstruction space.

Dimension counting was considered but yielded no signed rank estimate. The space contains E automatically; its large absolute dimension is irrelevant unless a class outside the kernel of the mass functional survives. Independent sampling of row tables does not make their truncated ideal subspaces independent random Grassmannian subspaces. No generic-rank, semiregularity or concentration assertion is made. Working retraction criterion and method controls; the global unit remains unresolved. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On near-half-family, develop the constant-cancellation attempt left by the previous entry. Can a row be removed from a putative unit identity by a linear conditional averaging map that does not increase degree, rather than by a chosen point substitution or an ungraded section?

New mathematics. An all-field criterion characterizes every degree-nonincreasing module retraction supported on a Boolean row: the product of its retained coordinates must not reduce to smaller degree on that row. This gives degree-exact deletion when the discarded coordinates are genuinely private. A binary all-parameter control has full conditional affine and single-quadratic moment surjectivity but no such filtered retraction. On the actual random-half source, replacing monomial-order tests by this exact criterion still causes the previously proved whole-context saturation.

Applying it through whole satisfiable contexts is defeated by saturation at the required cutoff. No odd-mass global separator or actual unit decomposition is obtained, and no formula-family upper bound or Frege transfer follows.

General statement. thm:filtered-row-retraction and cor:filtered-row-deletion cover arbitrary Boolean relations over any field. prop:conditional-moment-retraction-gap separates raw conditional ranks from the filtered map. cor:intrinsic-retraction-saturation applies the exact criterion to the original source using the already proved saturation theorem; ex:filtered-retraction-checks records finite rule checks.

Route comparison. Direct lower bounds still need the marked global unit. A private-row retraction could eliminate terms of a constant-valued identity without requiring all degree falls to vanish. This is a concrete method repair to test, not a new structural hardness axiom. The old ENS section-retraction and section-normal-form records supply the deletion mechanism in a special setting with constant private sections; both full proofs were reread. Here an arbitrary supported linear average is allowed and its exact filtration criterion is proved. The new method's failure on full random contexts is recorded immediately rather than refining its local ranks further.

Characterize the filtered module map

Let F be any field, let S and P be disjoint finite Boolean coordinate sets of sizes s and t, and let \(B=F[x_i:i\in S\cup P]/(x_i^2-x_i)\), \(A=F[x_i:i\in S]/(x_i^2-x_i)\). All degrees are those of unique multilinear representatives. Write \(x_T=\prod_{i\in T}x_i\), including \(x_\varnothing=1\), and \(B_{\le-1}=0\). Let \(R\subseteq\{0,1\}^{S\cup P}\), and let \(I(R)\) be its full Boolean vanishing ideal.

Theorem (filtered row retraction). The following are equivalent:

  1. There is an A-linear map \(T:B\to A\) with \(T(1)=1\), \(T(I(R))=0\), and \(\deg T(f)\le\deg f\) for every f.
  2. There is a multilinear \(w\in B\), supported on R, with \(\deg w\le t\), whose coefficient of \(x_P\) is one.
  3. No polynomial of degree at most \(s-1\) agrees with \(x_S\) on R.

Under the second condition the map is \(T(f)=\tau_P(wf)\), where multiplication is in B and \(\tau_P\) takes the coefficient of \(x_P\), leaving a polynomial in A. The map need not be an algebra homomorphism.

Trace pairing and all module maps. In one Boolean coordinate, the pairing taking the coefficient of x in a product has matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) on \(1,x\), of determinant minus one. Tensoring proves that \(\tau_P(uv)\) is a perfect A-bilinear pairing on the free A-module B. Thus every A-linear map has exactly one form \(T(f)=\tau_P(wf)\). Equivalently, at a fixed shared assignment a, \[T(f)(a)=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}^P}(-1)^{t-|b|}w(a,b)f(a,b).\tag{1}\] The signs are units over every field, including characteristic two. Testing the forbidden point indicators shows that \(T(I(R))=0\) exactly when w is zero off R.

The exact degree condition. Expand \(w=\sum_{Q\subseteq P}w_Q(x_S)x_Q\). For \(M\subseteq P\), Boolean multiplication gives \[T(x_M)=\sum_{Q\supseteq P\setminus M}w_Q.\tag{2}\] If \(\deg w\le t\), each summand on the right has degree at most \(t-|Q|\le|M|\). By A-linearity, multiplying by a shared monomial does not increase the required total degree, so T is filtered. Conversely, if T is filtered, start with \(M=\varnothing\) to see \(\deg w_P\le0\). Descend through subsets Q. In (2) take \(M=P\setminus Q\); all strict-superset coefficients have already been shown to have degree at most \(t-|Q|-1\). Since \(\deg T(x_M)\le|M|=t-|Q|\), it follows that \(\deg w_Q\le t-|Q|\). Hence \(\deg w\le t\). Also \(T(1)=w_P\), so the normalization is precisely \(w_P=1\). This proves equivalence of the first two conditions.

The monic-drop criterion. Let \(k=s+t\), and pair full Boolean functions by \(\tau_{S\cup P}(fg)\). This is nondegenerate by the same tensor calculation. Degree counting and binomial dimension symmetry give \[(B_{\le t})^\perp=B_{\le s-1}.\tag{3}\] The full point basis also gives \(I(R^c)^\perp=I(R)\), because \(I(R^c)\) is the space of functions supported on R and the trace pairing is diagonal on point indicators with nonzero signs. Therefore the annihilator of the allowed weight space is \[(B_{\le t}\cap I(R^c))^\perp=B_{\le s-1}+I(R).\tag{4}\] For \(\deg w\le t\), the pairing \(\tau_{S\cup P}(w x_S)\) is exactly the scalar \(w_P\): a term containing all private coordinates has no room for a positive shared degree. Thus a weight with \(w_P=1\) exists precisely when \(x_S\notin B_{\le s-1}+I(R)\), which is the third condition. A nonzero pairing is scaled to one. Empty coordinate sets and an empty relation are covered by the stated conventions. \(\square\)

The argument is a trace-duality refinement of the recorded local erasure duality, with an explicit marked coefficient and module filtration. It does not rely on positivity or a binary-only averaging convention. Local immunity through s suffices, but is stronger than necessary: the criterion tests only one monic degree drop. Existence implies that the projection of R onto S is the full cube, since otherwise a missing shared assignment indicator would give precisely such a drop.

What row deletion actually permits

Corollary (filtered row deletion). Add other coordinates Z, disjoint from S and P, and arbitrary ideals \(J_b\) in the Boolean algebra C on \(S\cup Z\). Extend all ideals to the Boolean algebra on \(S\cup P\cup Z\). If the theorem's criterion holds for R, then at every integer cutoff \(D\ge0\), \[\left[(I(R)B\cap B_{\le D})+\sum_b(J_bB\cap B_{\le D})\right]\cap C =\sum_b(J_b\cap C_{\le D}).\tag{5}\] Here B in (5) denotes the enlarged Boolean algebra. In particular a unit decomposition through D exists before deleting R if and only if one exists afterwards. This is a statement about these full row-ideal pieces; arbitrary original-generator NS cofactor bounds are not supplied.

Proof. Extend T by the identity on Z. It is C-linear, fixes C, and preserves total degree by the monomial proof above. It kills the extended row ideal I(R). For \(g\in J_bB\), expand in private monomials as \(g=\sum_{M\subseteq P}g_Mx_M\), where each \(g_M\in J_b\); this is the coefficientwise tensor description of an extended ideal. Then \(T(g)=\sum_Mg_MT(x_M)\in J_b\), while the degree does not exceed \(\deg g\). Apply T to a representation of any left-side element to obtain the right-side representation at the same cutoff. The reverse inclusion is immediate. \(\square\)

This extends the earlier constant-section deletion mechanism to all filtered module averages. Its privacy hypothesis is essential to this application: other row ideals must be extended from C. On the original random-half source, every coordinate occurs in at least two row scopes with high probability, so taking P to be genuinely private to one row leaves P empty. For a non-universal R the theorem then rejects deletion: the only A-linear unital map \(B=A\to A\) is the identity. This does not eliminate a row of the full source for free.

Raw conditional moments are insufficient

Proposition (conditional moment gap). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(s\ge3\), \(r\ge3\), take shared variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_s\) and private variables \(u_1,v_1,\ldots,u_r,v_r\), and define the allowed relation by \[x_1\cdots x_s=q(u,v),\qquad q=\sum_{j=1}^r u_jv_j.\tag{6}\] Every full shared assignment has a private fibre with full binary affine hull. On every such fibre, the constant, all private coordinate functions and any one squarefree quadratic in distinct private coordinates are linearly independent. Hence their moment map is onto. Nevertheless there is no filtered retraction fixing the shared Boolean algebra and killing I(R).

Conditional ranks. For the zero fibre of q, zero and all coordinate unit vectors prove full affine hull. For the one fibre, if an affine function vanishes there, fix one pair to \((1,1)\) and vary any coordinate from a different pair, keeping its partner zero and all other coordinates zero. This forces that coordinate's coefficient to vanish. For each coordinate choose a different fixed pair, and then the constant also vanishes. Thus this fibre too is affine-full.

To test an extra monomial ab in two distinct private coordinates, suppose an affine function plus \(c ab\) vanishes on \(q=\epsilon\). If a and b belong to different pairs, set both partners to zero and use a third pair with product epsilon. Vary a and b freely. This is an affine plane in the fibre, and its mixed difference forces c to be zero. If they belong to the same pair, copy a and b into another pair; the two products cancel. Use a third pair with product epsilon and again obtain an affine plane with a,b free. The same difference forces c to be zero. Affine fullness then kills the remaining coefficients. This proves all the claimed moment surjections without averaging by the even fibre sizes.

Filtered obstruction. Equation (6) identifies the retained monomial of degree s with a polynomial of degree two, less than s. It fails the exact criterion. Directly, a filtered retraction would give \(T(q)=x_1\cdots x_s\) while \(\deg T(q)\le2\), a contradiction. Raw point weights for each conditional moment specification exist by the proved ranks, but their dependence on the shared assignment cannot meet the necessary joint filtration. This is a satisfiable local relation, not a near-half formula-family obstruction or an exclusion of the central modular source. \(\square\)

The retraction itself is not required to preserve products. For example, on the three nonzero points of a two-bit cube, the binary weight one has mass one and defines a map to constants with \(T(x)=T(y)=0\) but \(T(xy)=1\). Thus this local averaging theorem does not construct the full Boolean variable action excluded by the earlier coefficient-fibre theorem.

The exact repair still saturates whole contexts

Corollary (intrinsic retraction saturation). Use the original random-half source with \(k=\lceil2\log_2v\rceil\), \(m=v+k\), and a fixed deterministic context seed of size \(\lfloor v/2-s_v\rfloor\), where \(s_v\ge0\), \(s_v=o(v/\sqrt{k})\). Suppose a monotone whole-context construction absorbs an entire row whenever no filtered retraction for that row can fix its currently retained coordinates \(S=X_a\cap C\). With probability \(1-o(1)\) this exact test grows the context to all v variables in two batches. If all contained rows are then imposed, the resulting context is unsatisfiable. No PC degree upper bound is asserted.

Proof with the existing probability theorem. The full saturation record was reread. On its simultaneous local interpolation event, every row function is represented through degree \(t_0=k-\lfloor k/2-\sqrt k\rfloor-1\). If \(|S|\ge t_0+1\), in particular \(x_S\) agrees on that row with a polynomial of degree at most \(t_0<|S|\). The new exact criterion therefore forbids every filtered retraction, not merely a particular monomial-order reduction. The proposed construction contains the old two-batch process with threshold \(t_0+1\). Its proved fixed-seed saturation and the unconditional good-source intersection give the conclusion. No new independence or adaptive-core claim is needed. \(\square\)

For every fixed \(\ell\ge2\), the specific cutoff deficit used in the current test, \(v/(\log(v+2))^{\ell-1}\), is in this range. Thus exact local retractions do not repair this whole-context architecture at that cutoff. They remain useful for genuinely private eliminations or differently organized coefficient calculations. The actual random family is not excluded. No specification restriction is adopted: the result is a method obstruction, not an upper bound on the family's PC degree.

9 October 2026 — Local filtration strengthens the specification without ensuring joint consistency

Working degree ceiling and non-vacuous refinement; termwise elimination fails its consistency test. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On near-half-family, test whether row-specific filtered eliminations can be applied term by term in one polynomial identity. Also extract the inexpensive structural consequence of the new exact row criterion, following the user's living guidance, before treating it only as a method observation.

New mathematics. The ordinary PC upper bound using local projection shattering strengthens to a field-dependent local filtration condition. A large selected set must admit a filtered retraction in every row separately. The existing guarded width-five family witnesses this stronger condition with unchanged costs and positive linear degree. Its already known guarded product identity now directly refutes automatic assembly of those row-specific retractions into a common linear map. The conditional quadratic relation gives a strict gap between the two local numerical parameters.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The new necessary condition has an unbounded witness, so it strengthens admissibility honestly, but supplies no near-half lower bound. Termwise elimination without a consistency argument fails. The original random and central sources are not excluded, and their satisfaction of the stronger near-half filtration condition has not been proved.

General statement. thm:filtered-shattering-ceiling is an all-field actual PC upper bound. prop:filtered-guarded-witness strengthens the existing witness and applies its existing product obstruction to the new maps. prop:projection-filtration-gap proves the new local parameter can be strictly smaller; ex:filtered-specification-checks checks the smallest instance. The guarded product itself is not claimed as new mathematics.

Route comparison. A direct global kernel remains the required construction. The termwise repair must first respect polynomial equalities, so the existing guarded control is tested before constructing more local sections. The structural corollary is cheap and retains the old witness; it is therefore adopted, with the unproved source application left explicit. Neither a local filtration condition nor its failure as a general gluing rule is identified with hardness of the source.

A stronger local parameter

For a canonical Boolean relation system over a proof field F, let \(R_a\) be its allowed rows on scopes \(X_a\), of maximum width w. Call \(S\subseteq[v]\) locally filtered if, for every row and \(U=S\cap X_a\), the monomial \(x_U\) has no representative of degree at most \(|U|-1\) on \(R_a\). Degrees and representatives are in that row's Boolean algebra. Equivalently, the exact retraction theorem says that the row admits an \(F[x_U]\)-linear unital degree-nonincreasing map to the retained coordinate algebra, annihilating its full row ideal. Let \(\rho_F\) be the maximum size of such S, with \(\rho_F=-1\) when an empty row makes even the empty set fail.

The parameter depends only on the stated finite row tables, incidence geometry and proof field, not on an unknown global proof space. Every locally filtered set is locally shattered: if a shared assignment is missing, its indicator has leading term a nonzero multiple of \(x_U\), with all other terms of smaller degree. Rescale that vanishing polynomial to obtain the prohibited lower-degree representative. Thus \(\rho_F\le\sigma\), where sigma is the earlier projection parameter.

Theorem (filtered shattering ceiling). For an unsatisfiable canonical Boolean relation system, \[d_F\le\max\{w,2,\rho_F+2\}.\tag{1}\] Consequently a barrier through \(D\ge\max\{w,2\}\) requires \(\rho_F\ge D-1\).

Proof. Assume the ordinary degree-D PC closure is proper. Its multilinear part is a proper cutoff kernel containing the inputs and closed under legal Boolean multiplication, by the paid Boolean reduction argument in the kernel-dimension proof. That proof gives more than linear injectivity: for a degree-compatible monomial order, there is a standard monomial \(x_S\) of degree exactly \(D-1\). In particular \(x_S\) is not congruent modulo that kernel to any polynomial of smaller total degree, even one using coordinates outside S.

Suppose some row violates the new condition, with \(U=S\cap X_a\). Write \(x_U-q\in I(R_a)\), with \(\deg q\le|U|-1\). In the canonical encoding the literal full-row indicator expansion derives this multilinear relation through original degree at most \(|X_a|\le w\le D\). Multiply its derived final line by \(x_{S\setminus X_a}\). The supports are disjoint and the final degree is \(D-1\), so the full derivation stays through \(\max\{w,D-1\}\le D\). It yields \[x_S-qx_{S\setminus X_a}\in C_D,\qquad \deg(qx_{S\setminus X_a})\le D-2,\] contradicting standardness. Hence S is locally filtered and \(\rho_F\ge D-1\). Taking \(D=\max\{w,2,\rho_F+2\}\) proves (1). The empty-row case is included by the canonical indicator derivation. \(\square\)

Using only the kernel theorem's ungraded coordinate injection would not justify this argument: a low-degree representative can involve outside variables. The degree-compatible standard-monomial part of its full proof is the relevant premise. Equation (1) refines the previous shattering ceiling without changing the width floor or its original-degree convention.

Non-vacuity and the termwise failure

Proposition (filtered guarded witness). The existing guarded width-five family has \(\rho_F=v-1\) over every field. It retains linear size, block minimality, essential scopes, at least two occurrences, branching fraction at least \(2/5\), full binary affine row hulls, no common Horn polarity and a positive-linear ordinary PC degree lower bound. Its rowwise filtered retractions need not respect joint polynomial identities when chosen term by term.

Construction and ledger. Use the already proved minimal branching family \(F_N\), with N variables, \(M=O(N)\) clauses of widths three or four, branching count \(h\ge2N/5\) and degree at least \(cN\). On disjoint copies x,y and one new guard t, take \[\{t\vee C(x):C\in F_N\}\cup\{\neg t\vee C(y):C\in F_N\}.\tag{2}\] There are exactly \(v=2N+1\) variables and \(2M\) clauses, of width at most five. Either guard value activates an unsatisfiable copy. Deleting one guarded clause allows its copy's deletion witness and disables the other copy, proving minimality. Every proper clause is essential; old occurrences are unchanged and t has \(2M\) occurrences. The branching fraction is \((2h+1)/(2N+1)\ge2/5\). Each row is the complement of one Boolean point and has full affine hull. If a common polarity made all clauses Horn, the copy with positive guard would have all remaining literals negative, making that old unsatisfiable copy satisfiable by zeros. Finally restricting one guard value and the unused copy in a PC refutation leaves a refutation of \(F_N\), so the new degree is at least \(cN=c(v-1)/2\). These are the original guarded witness's proved properties, with no changed encoding.

The stronger local condition. Select all non-guard coordinates S. In a row of the first copy, substitution \(t=1\) fixes all selected coordinates and annihilates its row ideal; in a row of the second, use \(t=0\). Both are unital module maps preserving degree. The exact row criterion gives local filtration on S, hence \(\rho_F\ge v-1\). The full set cannot qualify for a non-universal row: with no discarded coordinates the only linear module retraction fixing its whole coordinate algebra is the identity. Therefore \(\rho_F=v-1\). This proves unbounded non-vacuity of the stronger specification; it does not establish near-half degree.

The exact termwise consistency test. Let nonzero old clause polynomials be f(x) and g(y). The two guarded inputs are \((1-t)f\) and \(tg\), and their ordinary polynomial multiples satisfy \[(1-t)fg+tfg=fg.\tag{3}\] Every term has degree at most \(\deg f+\deg g+1\le9\). Extend each row retraction by the identity on all spectator coordinates. The first row's retraction sends its displayed multiple to zero, and the second row's retraction sends its multiple to zero. But both retractions fix the nonzero polynomial fg in the selected-coordinate algebra. Thus applying the row-specific map separately to each summand and fixing selected-coordinate polynomials is not a well-defined linear operation on the polynomial represented by that sum. No common linear map on these lines can both kill the two multiples and fix fg.

This reuses the old guarded product as a control for the newly proposed maps. A correct global kernel is allowed to contain fg while retaining one; (3) does not itself refute the family. It rejects the stronger termwise rule that keeps the entire selected algebra fixed. Consequently local filtration is an admissibility screen, not a substitute for global compatibility, and the positive-linear witness remains consistent with the obstruction.

The strengthening is strict already locally

Proposition (projection filtration gap). For the binary relation \[R=\{(x,u,v):x_1\cdots x_s=\sum_{j=1}^r u_jv_j\},\qquad s,r\ge3,\quad k=s+2r,\tag{4}\] the maximum locally shattered coordinate set has size \(\sigma=k-2\), but \(\rho_{\mathbb F_2}\le k-3\). This is a satisfiable single-row control, not a new unsatisfiable-family claim.

Classify the maximal projections. Omitting both coordinates of one private pair leaves a full projection: its product can be selected as either zero or one to satisfy (4). No projection omitting only one coordinate is full. If the omitted coordinate is shared, set another retained shared bit to zero and the private sum to one. If it is private, set its retained partner to zero, another complete pair's product to one and the shared product to zero.

Among projections omitting exactly two coordinates, the same-pair omissions are the only full ones. If both omitted coordinates are shared, at least one retained shared coordinate remains and can be set to zero while the private sum is one. If one is shared and one private, set another shared coordinate and the omitted private coordinate's partner to zero and a different pair's product to one. If two private coordinates from different pairs are omitted, set both retained partners to zero and a third pair's product to one, again with shared product zero. These assignments have no extension. Thus \(\sigma=k-2\), and every set achieving that size omits a full private pair.

For such a set S, omitting pair j, multiply (4) by the product H of all other private coordinates. On R this gives \[x_S=(r-1)H+H u_jv_j.\tag{5}\] The scalar is taken in the binary field. The right side has degree at most \(2r<s+2r-2=|S|\). Every maximally shattered set therefore fails the filtered criterion. Since filtration implies shattering, \(\rho_{\mathbb F_2}\le k-3\). \(\square\)

The exact control takes the smallest \(s=r=3\). Among 512 assignments it finds 280 allowed points; all 36 seven-coordinate projections and all nine eight-coordinate projections are checked. Precisely the three complete-private-pair omissions give full seven-coordinate projections, and none of the eight-coordinate projections is full. All 840 pointwise instances of (5) pass. This verifies the strict \(\sigma=7,\rho\le6\) control, not a near-half lower bound.

Specification decision and research outcome

9 October 2026 — Large independent sets rule out the actual Kneser cores

Working characteristic-two degree ceiling; the queued compact Kneser-core family is excluded. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On near-half-family, develop the Kneser/core head. The missing implication is a near-half PC barrier on an actual unbounded source. The previous full-graph topological bound did not address edge-minimal cores. Test whether independent sets inherited by every such core, combined with paid star projection, give an upper bound in the core's own Boolean variable count.

New mathematics. Compact four-colouring on a non-four-colourable N-vertex graph with independent set I has binary PC degree at most \(\lfloor3(N-|I|)/2\rfloor+2\). After eliminating I, fixing the first boundary bits turns each star determinant into a product of linear forms on disjoint second-bit groups. Conditioning the smaller group leaves inconsistent binary affine equations. Every actual core of the recorded Kneser source therefore has degree at most \(3v/8+o(v)\), on its own \(v=2N\) bits. The argument also covers non-four-colourable graphs mapping homomorphically to that source.

Goal progress. Unchanged for the general near-half-family obligation: this is a decisive exclusion of the queued candidate, not a construction of the missing family. It resolves the previously open scope issue for those cores by a different argument, without transferring a full-graph proof backwards. Complete Frege transfer remains open.

General statement. lem:bipartite-product-ceiling gives the paid affine-product branch certificate. thm:independent-colour-degree-ceiling is an all-graph upper bound in the stated encoding. cor:kneser-core-degree-ceiling applies to all actual cores and homomorphic replacements. cor:colour-independence-screen records the necessary graph condition; prop:compact-colour-filtration explains why the latest local specification does not itself exclude these graphs. ex:independent-colour-compiler-checks records complete bounded certificates.

Route comparison. A direct lower-bound construction on these cores is worth pursuing only if their inherited independent-set geometry survives the explicit projection test. The crude full-assignment bound after projection remains above half, so it would not settle anything. The second-bit product structure below supplies the missing gain. No universal half-variable bound for arbitrary Boolean polynomial systems is assumed, and no topological premise on the deleted-edge cores is used.

Two groups of affine products

Work over any characteristic-two proof field F, but let all coefficients of the following affine inputs lie in its binary prime subfield. Split Boolean variables into disjoint sets X,Y, of sizes a,b. Inputs may be arbitrary affine equations solely in X, arbitrary affine equations solely in Y, and products \(L_i(X)M_i(Y)\) of such binary affine forms, together with Booleanity.

Lemma (bipartite product ceiling). If this system has no Boolean solution, it has an ordinary Nullstellensatz refutation, hence a PC refutation, through degree at most \(\min(a,b)+2\).

Proof. Suppose \(a\le b\) and fix \(\alpha\in\{0,1\}^X\). A left affine input may become a nonzero constant; otherwise the residual equations in Y are the original right affine equations and those \(M_i\) with \(L_i(\alpha)=1\). They are inconsistent over the binary field: consistency would give a binary solution, hence a Boolean model of the full restricted system. Therefore a binary linear combination of these affine inputs equals one. This remains a valid identity in F.

Put \(\delta_\alpha=\prod_{j\in X}(x_j+1-\alpha_j)\), of degree a. For a binary affine L, \[\delta_\alpha(L-L(\alpha))=\sum_{j\in X}L_j(x_j^2-x_j)\prod_{h\in X\setminus\{j\}}(x_h+1-\alpha_h),\tag{1}\] where \(L_j\) is the coefficient of \(x_j\); signs coincide in characteristic two. Multiplying (1) by \(M_i(Y)\) costs at most \(a+2\). Thus every weighted residual affine equation is an ordinary combination of original inputs and Boolean-axiom multiples through \(a+2\). The residual linear certificate gives \(\delta_\alpha\), including the constant-input case. Sum all \(\delta_\alpha\) to one. This is a literal NS identity at that degree. Interchange X,Y for the stated minimum. \(\square\)

The binary-coefficient hypothesis is used when affine consistency is equated with a Boolean solution. No assertion for arbitrary extension-field affine coefficients is needed. This is a paid conditioning-and-linear-elimination mechanism, not a new general Gaussian-elimination principle.

Project an independent set, then split the palette

Let G be a finite simple graph with N nonisolated vertices, not four-colourable. Its original variables are two bits \((u_i,v_i)\) per vertex; each edge has the four canonical equal-colour forbidden clauses. Fix any independent set I, put \(B=V(G)\setminus I\) and \(b=|B|\). Necessarily \(b\ge4\), since otherwise distinct colours on B and one additional colour on I would suffice.

Theorem (independent colour ceiling). Over every characteristic-two proof field, \[d_F(G)\le b+\lfloor b/2\rfloor+2=\lfloor3b/2\rfloor+2.\tag{2}\] In particular choose I maximum, so \(b=N-\alpha(G)\). No polynomial proof-size bound or reverse projection simulation is asserted.

First use the already paid projection. On the \(2b\) boundary bits retain the edge quadratics \[q_{ij}=(1+u_i+u_j)(1+v_i+v_j),\qquad ij\in E(G[B]),\] and, for every centre \(c\in I\) and four-subset U of its neighbours, retain \[\Delta_U=\det[(1,u_i,v_i,u_iv_i)]_{i\in U}.\tag{3}\] The star-projection proof and its common-boundary composition were read in full. Independence of I makes the boundary system exactly the extendible-colouring relation, hence unsatisfiable. Each displayed input has an ordinary derivation through degree four from the original CNF. In detail, writing a star equation as the matrix row \(((1+u_i)(1+v_i),1+v_i,1+u_i,1)\) times \((1,u_c,v_c,u_cv_c)^T\), the first adjugate row gives \(\Delta_U\) as a sum of degree-two cofactors times star quadratics. This pays degree four; the quadratics themselves are derived through four from the canonical clauses. Final lines are reused.

Fix the first bits. For \(\eta\in\{0,1\}^B\), split B into \(B_0,B_1\) according to the first bit. A boundary edge becomes zero when its ends lie in different groups, and becomes \(1+v_i+v_j\) within one group. For a four-neighbour determinant, if its first bits are not split two and two, its restricted polynomial is identically zero. If \(U=\{i,j\}\sqcup\{h,l\}\) with \(i,j\in B_0\) and \(h,l\in B_1\), then literally \[\Delta_U|_\eta=(v_i+v_j)(v_h+v_l).\tag{4}\] This follows by grouping the two types of matrix rows in (3) and subtracting one row from the other in each pair. It is also a multilinear polynomial identity, not only equality after Boolean reduction. Thus the restricted system is exactly of the preceding lemma's type, on the two disjoint second-bit groups. Its degree ceiling is \(\min(|B_0|,|B_1|)+2\le\lfloor b/2\rfloor+2\).

Pay both stages without flattening the first. Write \(\delta_\eta\) for the first-bit point indicator, of degree b. For every boundary input g of degree at most four, derive \(\delta_\eta g|_\eta\) through degree at most \(b+4\). To see the Boolean cost explicitly, replace the first-bit variables one at a time in g. Multilinearity gives \[g-g|_\eta=\sum_i(u_i-\eta_i)h_i,\qquad \deg h_i\le\deg g-1.\] Multiplication by \(\delta_\eta\) replaces each \(u_i-\eta_i\) factor by its Boolean polynomial times the indicator on the other first bits, exactly as in (1). Every correction has degree at most \(b+\deg g\le b+4\). The final weighted residual inputs have degree at most \(b+2\).

Now use the lemma's proof on the smaller second-bit group, with all its lines multiplied by \(\delta_\eta\). Its starting weighted inputs are the just-derived final lines. Multiplying them by the smaller group's indicator and using the same Boolean corrections costs at most \(b+\min(|B_0|,|B_1|)+2\). The affine certificate then gives \(\delta_\eta\). Weighted Boolean inputs are obtained directly from the original Boolean axioms within this budget. Since \(b\ge4\), both the initial ceiling \(b+4\) and every branch ceiling fit \(b+\lfloor b/2\rfloor+2\). Sum \(\delta_\eta\) over all first-bit assignments to obtain one. This proves (2).

The reuse is essential to the stated ledger: multiplying the entire first-stage proof by every second-bit indicator would give an unnecessarily larger bound. The theorem is an ordinary PC ceiling. It does not claim that flattening both stages into one original-input NS identity preserves (2).

Inventory. The original CNF has \(2N\) actual bits and \(4|E(G)|\) width-four clauses. The boundary has at most \(\binom b2+\sum_{c\in I}\binom{\deg(c)}4=O(N^5)\) polynomial inputs, of degree at most four and support at most eight bits, with no new variables. Unused boundary bits may be removed, but counting all \(2b\) only weakens the bound. No free canonical-CNF conversion of the boundary polynomials is used. The proof is replayed on the original system after its degree-four input derivations.

The core exclusion and what it teaches

Corollary (Kneser core ceiling). Let G be any non-four-colourable graph on N nonisolated vertices admitting a graph homomorphism to \(KG(n,k)\), with \(k\ge1\) and \(n\ge2k\). Then its compact four-colour CNF satisfies \[d_F(G)\le\left\lfloor\frac32\left(N-\left\lceil\frac{kN}{n}\right\rceil\right)\right\rfloor+2\tag{5}\] over every characteristic-two proof field. In particular every recorded edge-minimal core of \(KG(2k+4,k)\), with its isolated vertices removed and \(v=2N\), satisfies \[d_F(G)\le\frac{3v}{8}+\frac{3v}{4(k+2)}+2 =\frac{3v}{8}+o(v)\qquad(k\to\infty).\tag{6}\] It cannot meet the near-half target.

Proof. For each ground element j, the vertices whose image k-set contains j form an independent set: adjacent image sets are disjoint. Each vertex occurs in exactly k of these n sets, even when the homomorphism is not injective. One such independent set therefore has size at least \(\lceil kN/n\rceil\). Apply (2). At \(n=2k+4\), its continuous bound is \(3N/4+3N/(2(k+2))+2\), giving (6). The recorded cores have \(N\ge2\lceil k/4\rceil+1\to\infty\), so the constant term is negligible. This is a bound on each core itself, not a reverse transfer from the full graph. \(\square\)

More generally, any unbounded homomorphic family with \(n/k\le3-\varepsilon\), for a fixed positive epsilon, has a fixed gap below half its \(2N\) bits by (5). Thus replacing the original core by a high-girth graph that still maps to the same near-two-ratio Kneser graph does not evade the reason for the bound. Long odd girth, minimality and strong local row properties do not cancel its inherited independent-set cover.

Corollary (colour independence screen). If a compact four-colour family has no refutation through \(D=\lfloor N-s\rfloor\), with \(s\ge0\), then \[\alpha(G)<\frac N3+\frac{2s}{3}+\frac43.\tag{7}\] Hence a near-half family must have \(\limsup\alpha(G)/N\le1/3\). A fractional colouring of total weight \(t<3\) bounded away from three also rules it out asymptotically.

Proof. Integer degree greater than \(\lfloor N-s\rfloor\) is greater than \(N-s\). Compare this with \(\frac32(N-\alpha)+2\) and rearrange. If nonnegative weights on independent sets cover each vertex by total weight at least one and have total t, then \(N\le\sum_I\lambda_I|I|\le t\alpha\); thus \(\alpha\ge N/t\), giving the last claim. \(\square\)

Specification disposition. This is a new necessary condition for the compact four-colour sub-specification. Its conjunction with all existing graph screens does not yet have a proved unbounded witness here, so it is provisional rather than an adopted non-vacuity assertion. The earlier high-girth critical-graph construction did not control its independence ratio after selecting a minimal core. The general guarded formula specification is unaffected and retains its witness.

The structural reason also applies to other four-colouring candidates with an independent-set cover of total weight below three; it is not specific to the Kneser presentation. The earlier two-anchor graphs are already excluded more strongly by their degree-six proof. The modular and random-relation candidates do not have this graph encoding, so no transfer to them is asserted. Raising the Kneser ground-set ratio to at least three would evade this particular fixed-gap argument, but loses the old growing-odd-girth justification of unbounded cores and does not supply a replacement hardness proof. Adding a common palette anchor instead reduces to the already excluded three-colour setting. A stronger replacement must establish its own actual core-size, independence and degree budgets.

The local filtration screen alone does not see this obstruction

Proposition (compact colour filtration). For the canonical proper-colouring relation on \(2^b\) states, with an integer \(b\ge1\) bits per vertex and any proof field, every proper subset of an edge's \(2b\) bits admits a degree-preserving row retraction. The full set does not. Consequently for a graph on N declared vertices, \[\rho_F=\sigma=(b-1)N+\alpha(G).\tag{8}\] In particular compact four-colouring always has \(\rho_F\ge N\), so its local filtration condition alone cannot exclude a barrier just below N.

Proof. Choose a missing bit at one endpoint. If the corresponding bit at the other endpoint is retained, set the missing one to its complement. If that other bit is also missing, set the two to opposite constants. Set any remaining discarded bits to constants. This affine substitution fixes every retained bit and always produces unequal endpoint colours; it is a unital degree-preserving algebra retraction annihilating the row ideal. The full coordinate set cannot retract through a non-universal relation. Its projection likewise is not full, whereas every proper projection extends by the same construction.

Thus a selected set of bits qualifies exactly when the vertices with all b bits selected form an independent set. At every other vertex at most \(b-1\) bits are selected, giving the upper bound in (8); choose a maximum independent set in full and \(b-1\) bits at every other vertex to attain it. For actual-variable applications discard isolated graph vertices first. \(\square\)

This is another reason to retain actual upper-bound screens across equivalent paid representations: the newly strengthened local admissibility test still allows the Kneser cores that (6) rules out globally.

It then removes the four independent clone vertices from the Mycielski graph of the complete four-vertex graph. The five-vertex boundary has six edge quadratics and four star determinants.

All 32 first-bit assignments and all 102 smaller-side second-bit branches yield native binary affine certificates. The full branch certificates are retained in the output. Two initial script errors—a reserved identifier and polynomial constants not converted to native matrix entries—are retained separately. Only the corrected run reached the final success marker. These checks validate the compiler, not an asymptotic lower bound or an enumeration of growing cores.
