General statement. lem:shared-pin-drop holds for all modular rows through one variable over every proof field of characteristic different from the modulus. thm:derived-relation-ceiling is an all-field statement for arbitrary unsatisfiable Boolean systems. thm:shared-pin-degree-ceiling covers every regular even-width modular system, cor:paired-source-depth-exclusion applies it to the source law, and prop:row-rule-nonconfluence records the rewriting consequence. ex:pair-join-controls is the finite control.

Setting and the dependency used

Fix an odd prime \(q\) and a proof field \(F\) of characteristic different from \(q\); the binary field is the case of interest. Let \(\mathcal B=F[x_1,\ldots,x_v]/(x_i^2-x_i)\) with its multilinear representatives and degree filtration. A modular row \(a\) has scope \(X_a\), nonzero coefficients \(a_i\in\mathbb F_q^\times\), a target, allowed Boolean set \(R_a\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X_a}\), and cylinder ideal \(J_a\subseteq\mathcal B\) of functions vanishing on \(R_a\times\{0,1\}^{[v]\setminus X_a}\). The system is encoded by the forbidden-tuple clauses of each row, of width \(|X_a|\), with Booleanity. Write \(C_D\) for its ordinary degree-\(D\) PC closure and \(K_D=\sum_a(J_a\cap\mathcal B_{\le D})\).

The only imported statement is the modular row interpolation lemma (lem:modular-row-interpolation), reread with its proof: for a row of width \(k\) with nonzero coefficients, every monomial on its scope of degree greater than \(k/2\) has, modulo the row's vanishing ideal, a representative of strictly smaller degree. This holds for every target, central or not, and trivially for an empty relation.

Local derivability. If \(w\) bounds all row widths, then \(J_a\cap\mathcal B_{\le M}\subseteq C_{\max\{w,M\}}\). Indeed expand \(g\in J_a\) by monomials \(u\) in the variables outside \(X_a\): \(g=\sum_u u\,g_u\), where each \(g_u\) is a function on \(X_a\) vanishing on \(R_a\), and \(\deg g=\max_u(|u|+\deg g_u)\) because distinct outside monomials cannot cancel. Each \(g_u\) is a scalar combination of forbidden-tuple indicators, which are axioms of degree \(|X_a|\le w\). Multiplying \(g_u\) by the variables of \(u\) one at a time raises the degree by exactly one per step, ending at \(|u|+\deg g_u\le M\). Hence \(K_M\subseteq C_{\max\{w,M\}}\).

Two rows through one unselected variable

Lemma (shared-pin drop). Let rows \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\), \(n\ge1\), all contain a variable \(x\), with widths \(k_i\). Let \(T_i\subseteq X_{a_i}\setminus\{x\}\) be pairwise disjoint with \(|T_i|>(k_i-1)/2\), put \(T=\bigcup_iT_i\), and let \(S\supseteq T\) be any set of variables with \(x\notin S\). Then there is a polynomial \(r\) with

\[x_S-r\in K_{|S|},\qquad \deg r\le|S|-n+1.\tag{1}\]

In particular, for \(n\ge2\) the monomial \(x_S\) has a representative of smaller degree modulo \(C_{\max\{w,|S|\}}\).

Proof. Fix \(i\) and \(c\in\{0,1\}\). Substituting \(x=c\) in row \(a_i\) leaves a modular row on the \(k_i-1\) other variables with the same nonzero coefficients and a shifted target. Since \(|T_i|>(k_i-1)/2\), the interpolation lemma gives a polynomial \(p_{i,c}\) on \(X_{a_i}\setminus\{x\}\) with \(\deg p_{i,c}\le|T_i|-1\) and \(x_{T_i}=p_{i,c}\) on \(R_{a_i}\cap\{x=c\}\). Put \(q_i=(1-x)p_{i,0}+x\,p_{i,1}\). Then \(g_i=x_{T_i}-q_i\) is a function on \(X_{a_i}\) vanishing on \(R_{a_i}\), so \(g_i\in J_{a_i}\), and \(\deg q_i\le|T_i|\). The telescoping identity

\[\prod_{i=1}^n x_{T_i}-\prod_{i=1}^n q_i=\sum_{j=1}^n\Bigl(\prod_{i<j}q_i\Bigr)g_j\Bigl(\prod_{i>j}x_{T_i}\Bigr)\tag{2}\]

holds in \(\mathcal B\). Its \(j\)-th summand lies in \(J_{a_j}\) and has degree at most \(\sum_i|T_i|=|T|\), since \(\deg q_i\le|T_i|\), \(\deg g_j\le|T_j|\) and multilinear reduction never raises degree. Because \(1-x\) and \(x\) are orthogonal idempotents, \(\prod_iq_i=(1-x)\prod_ip_{i,0}+x\prod_ip_{i,1}\), of degree at most \(1+\sum_i(|T_i|-1)=|T|-n+1\). The left product is \(x_T\) by disjointness. Multiply (2) by \(x_{S\setminus T}\): each summand stays in its cylinder ideal with degree at most \(|S|\), and \(r=x_{S\setminus T}\prod_iq_i\) has degree at most \(|S|-n+1\). \(\square\)

Neither product structure of the join nor disjointness of the scopes is used: two congruences that hold on two cylinders hold on their intersection. Disjointness of the \(T_i\) is needed only so that the left side of (2) has degree \(|T|\). For \(n=1\) the statement is the trivial identity \(x_{T_1}\equiv q_1\) of equal degree, which is why a single row keeps its half. The hypothesis \(x\notin S\) is a convenience: only \(x\notin T_i\) is used, and for \(x\in S\setminus T\) the same proof gives \(\deg r\le|S|-n\).

What fails for a selected shared variable. The lemma cannot be applied with \(x\) in a trace: removing \(x\) from a half leaves \(h-1\) variables, below the threshold. Concretely, if \(x\in S\), write \(x_S=x\cdot x_{S\setminus x}\). On the fibre \(x=1\) each row contributes \(|T_i\setminus\{x\}|\), and the count \(1+\sum_i(|T_i|-1)\) equals \(|S\cap\bigcup_iX_{a_i}|\) when \(x\) lies in every \(T_i\); no drop follows. For paired rows meeting in a variable of the selected part \(L\), the two preferred completions use disjoint sets of partners and combine into one affine retraction of the join, so the monomial on all retained \(L\)-coordinates is irreducible there. The control below confirms both sides.

The row-rule family is not confluent

Fix a degree-compatible monomial order. The row-rule family rewrites a monomial \(u\,m\), where \(m\) is a leading monomial of the vanishing ideal of one row on its scope and \(u\) is a monomial in the other variables, to \(u\) times the row normal form of \(m\). This is the multilinear analogue, built from the actual row relations, of the reduction systems in the bounded normal-form proposition. Only three facts from there are used, and they hold here by the same arguments: reduction terminates, unique normal forms are equivalent to joinability of all local peaks, and unique normal forms give a linear normal-form map killing every rule instance. Its rule instances of degree at most \(M\) span exactly \(K_M\), because a degree-compatible Gröbner basis of one row reduces every element of \(J_a\cap\mathcal B_{\le M}\) to zero without raising degree.

Proposition (row-rule nonconfluence). In the setting of the lemma with \(n\ge2\), suppose \(x_S\) is irreducible for the row-rule family. Then that family does not have unique normal forms on \(\mathcal B_{\le|S|}\); equivalently some local peak of degree at most \(|S|\) has no common reduct inside \(\mathcal B_{\le|S|}\). For the paired source this happens in degree \(k\) on the good event of the corollary below: use the degree-lexicographic order with every \(R\)-variable above every \(L\)-variable, two rows \(a,b\) meeting exactly in a variable \(x\) of the part \(R\), and \(S=L\cap(X_a\cup X_b)\). Such rows exist there, because fewer than \(v/2\) variables fail to be clean and a clean variable of \(R\) lies on nine rows.

Proof. Reduce \(r\) in (1) by row rules to a polynomial \(r'\) supported on irreducible monomials; the degree does not increase, so \(\deg r'\le|S|-1\) and \(x_S-r'\in K_{|S|}\) is a nonzero polynomial supported on irreducible monomials. If normal forms were unique on \(\mathcal B_{\le|S|}\), the normal-form map would be linear, would kill every rule instance and hence \(K_{|S|}\), and would fix \(x_S-r'\); contradiction. For a terminating reduction relation, failure of unique normal forms is equivalent to an unjoinable local peak, by the well-founded induction recorded in the bounded normal-form proposition. In the paired example, every monomial on \(L\cap X_a\) is standard for row \(a\) in the stated order: the paired retraction maps a relation with that leading monomial to a nonzero polynomial on the free \(L\)-cube, since every other term is either an \(L\)-monomial of the same degree or has smaller degree. In the stated order a monomial containing an \(R\)-variable exceeds every \(L\)-monomial of its degree. For every row \(c\) of the system, \(S\cap X_c\subseteq L\cap X_c\) is therefore standard, so no row rule applies to \(x_S\). \(\square\)

The peak is cutoff-legal for every \(D\ge k\). It rejects the row-rule family, not hardness. Adjoining the relations (1) as new rules is forced on any proper kernel, since \(K_{|S|}\subseteq C_D\); the next two results measure what is left after that completion.

A ceiling from relations derived inside the cutoff

Theorem (derived-relation ceiling). Let an unsatisfiable Boolean polynomial system, with Booleanity, have axioms of degree at most \(w\) over any field. Let \(E\ge1\) and \(D\ge\max\{w,E+1\}\). Suppose that for every \(E\)-subset \(S\) of the variables there is \(r_S\) with \(\deg r_S\le E-1\) and \(x_S-r_S\in C_D\). Then \(1\in C_D\).

Proof. Put \(W=\mathcal B_{\le E-1}\) and \(Q=C_D\cap W\).

Reduction. Every \(f\in\mathcal B_{\le D}\) has some \(\rho(f)\in W\) with \(f-\rho(f)\in C_D\). For a monomial \(x_T\) with \(E\le|T|\le D\), choose an \(E\)-subset \(S\subseteq T\). The polynomial \(x_S-r_S\in C_D\) has degree at most \(E\), and multiplying it by the \(|T|-E\) variables of \(T\setminus S\) one at a time meets degrees at most \(|T|-1\le D-1\) before the last step, so \(x_{T\setminus S}(x_S-r_S)\in C_D\). Thus \(x_T\) is congruent modulo \(C_D\) to \(x_{T\setminus S}r_S\), of degree at most \(|T|-1\); induct on degree and extend linearly. Two choices of \(\rho(f)\) differ by an element of \(Q\).

Operators. On \(M=W/Q\) define \(T_i[f]=[\rho(x_if)]\); here \(\deg x_if\le E\le D\). If \(f\in Q\) then \(x_if\in C_D\) because \(\deg f\le D-1\), so \(\rho(x_if)\in Q\); hence \(T_i\) is a well-defined linear map. For \(f\in W\), the polynomial \(x_jf-\rho(x_jf)\in C_D\) has degree at most \(E\le D-1\), so its product with \(x_i\) lies in \(C_D\) and \(T_iT_j[f]=[\rho(x_ix_jf)]\). This is symmetric in \(i,j\), and equals \(T_i[f]\) when \(i=j\). The \(T_i\) are commuting idempotents, so \(M\) is a module over \(\mathcal B\).

Monomials. For a monomial \(m\) of degree \(n\le D\) with variables \(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_n}\), induction gives \(T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_n}[1]=[\rho(m)]\): if \(m=x_{i_1}m'\), then \(m'-\rho(m')\in C_D\) has degree at most \(n-1\le D-1\), so \(x_{i_1}\rho(m')\equiv m\) modulo \(C_D\). Hence every polynomial \(A\) of degree at most \(D\) acts by \(A\cdot[1]=[\rho(A)]\).

Conclusion. \(M\) is generated by \([1]\), so \(M\cong\mathcal B/\mathfrak a\) for the annihilator \(\mathfrak a\) of \([1]\). Every axiom \(A\) has degree at most \(w\le D\) and lies in \(C_D\), so \(\rho(A)\in Q\) and \(A\in\mathfrak a\). The axioms generate the unit ideal of \(\mathcal B\) because the system has no Boolean solution. Therefore \(1\in\mathfrak a\), that is \([1]=0\) and \(1\in Q\subseteq C_D\). \(\square\)

This extends the local interpolation ceiling (prop:local-interpolation-degree-ceiling), whose relations come from one row, to any relations already derived within the cutoff, with the same quotient-operator proof; that proposition is the case in which each \(x_S-r_S\) is a spectator multiple of a single-row relation. The underlying principle is the known bound of solving degree by degree of regularity plus one, as cited there. No novelty is claimed for it.

The double count

Consider an unsatisfiable modular system in which every row has the same even width \(k=2h\), all coefficients are nonzero, and every variable lies in exactly \(r\ge1\) rows. It has \(m=rv/k\) rows. Call a variable clean if any two distinct rows containing it meet only in it, and let \(\beta\) be the number of variables that are not clean. Put

\[c^*=\frac{(r-1)(v/2-\beta)}{rh+1},\qquad E=\lfloor v/2-c^*\rfloor+1.\tag{3}\]

Theorem (shared-pin ceiling). If \(1\le E\le v\), the canonical encoding has an ordinary PC refutation over \(F\) of degree at most \(\max\{k,E+1\}=\max\{k,\lfloor v/2-c^*\rfloor+2\}\).

Proof. Let \(S\) be an \(E\)-subset and \(s_a=|S\cap X_a|\). We produce \(r_S\) of degree at most \(E-1\) with \(x_S-r_S\in K_E\subseteq C_{\max\{k,E\}}\), and then apply the derived-relation ceiling with \(w=k\) and \(D=\max\{k,E+1\}\).

If some \(s_a\ge h+1\), the interpolation lemma lowers \(x_{S\cap X_a}\) modulo \(J_a\), and multiplication by \(x_{S\setminus X_a}\) gives the relation. If a clean variable \(x\notin S\) lies on two rows \(a,b\) with \(s_a=s_b=h\), apply the shared-pin drop with \(n=2\), \(T_a=S\cap X_a\), \(T_b=S\cap X_b\): these avoid \(x\), are disjoint because \(X_a\cap X_b=\{x\}\), and have size \(h>(k-1)/2\).

Suppose neither case occurs. Then every \(s_a\le h\); call a row full when \(s_a=h\). Summing over rows, \(\sum_as_a=rE\), so the number of rows that are not full is at most \(mh-rE=r(v/2-E)\). Writing \(c'=v/2-E\), the number \(f\) of full rows satisfies \(f\ge m-rc'\). Each full row contains exactly \(h\) variables outside \(S\). A clean variable outside \(S\) lies on at most one full row, and any variable lies on at most \(r\) rows, so counting incidences between full rows and outside variables gives

\[h(m-rc')\le hf\le(v-E)+(r-1)\beta=v/2+c'+(r-1)\beta.\]

Since \(hm=rv/2\), this is \(c'(rh+1)\ge(r-1)(v/2-\beta)\), that is \(c'\ge c^*\). But \(E>v/2-c^*\) means \(c'

No centrality, pairing or layer structure is used. For \(r=1\) the theorem holds but gives \(c^*=0\), as it must: one partition of central paired rows keeps the monomial on \(L\).

The paired source

Corollary (paired depth exclusion). With probability \(1-o(1)\), the balanced paired source with \(v=l2^l\), \(k=16l\), nine layers and prime \(v^2 \[d_2\le\frac v2-\frac{4v-8k^3}{9h+1}+2=\frac v2-\Bigl(\frac89-o(1)\Bigr)\frac vk.\tag{4}\]

Consequently a barrier through \(D=\lfloor v/2-s\rfloor\) on the original instance needs \(s\ge(8/9-o(1))v/k=\Omega(v/\log v)\). Since \(k=16l\le16\log_2v\), this contradicts \(s=o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\) for every \(\ell\ge3\). It does not contradict \(s=o(v)\), the requirement at \(\ell=2\).

Proof. On the source's good event the system is unsatisfiable with nonzero coefficients, every row has width \(k\) and every variable lies in nine rows, one per layer. It remains to bound \(\beta\). Let \(N_2\) count unordered pairs of variables that share a row in two different layers; a variable that is not clean belongs to such a pair, so \(\beta\le2N_2\). Fix two variables and a layer. If both lie in the same part, the probability that the uniform partition of that part puts them in one block is \((h-1)/(v/2-1)

The same theorem applies to the five- and nine-partition independent central sources once their non-clean variables are counted; those were already excluded at \(\ell\ge3\) by the pairing criterion, so nothing new is claimed for them.

What the bound teaches

Structural reason. Half-width interpolation of an even central row is a parity effect: after one coordinate is pinned the row has odd width and loses the top degree. A fractional cover charges a pin once but, when the pinned variable is not selected, every row through it drops. The common filtered half \(L\) is locally optimal in each row and globally the worst choice, since every variable of \(R\) lies on nine full rows. The fractional row ceiling could not see this because it uses one row per monomial.

Other candidates. The reason applies to every regular canonical modular source with even rows and at least two rows through each variable, whatever the coefficient law. It does not apply to rows whose one-pin residuals keep interpolation degree \(k/2\); modular rows cannot have this property, by odd width. Raising the width beyond a constant times \((\log v)^{\ell-2}\) would evade (4), but the canonical encoding of a width-\(k\) row has \(2^k\) clauses, so for \(\ell\ge3\) the encoding stops being polynomial. A modular source for \(\ell\ge3\) would therefore need a different, paid row encoding, and the variable count of that encoding enters the half.

Whether the mechanism reaches linear deficit. Everything in this paragraph is unverified. The lemma should generalize: for a set \(Z\) of pinned variables outside \(S\) and any rows \(G\), \(x_S\) has the lower-degree representative \(\sum_c\mathbf 1_{Z=c}\prod_ap_{a,c}\) whenever \(|S\cap\bigcup_{a\in G}X_a|>|Z|+\sum_{a\in G}t_a\), where \(t_a\) bounds the interpolation degree of row \(a\) after pinning \(Z\cap X_a\); the telescoping proof shows derivability inside degree \(|S|\) only for disjoint traces with \(|Z\cap X_a|+t_a\le|T_a|\), and the general derivation cost is not established. The left side counts the union, so the traces \(S\cap X_a\) must be nearly disjoint while the pinned variables are shared. A row with deficit \(e_a=h-s_a\ge1\) and \(z_a\) pinned variables contributes at most \(\lfloor z_a/2\rfloor+1-e_a\) when its residual is noncentral. For rows of deficit one this needs two pins per row and more than two rows per pin, that is two independent cycles of rows joined through unselected variables with disjoint selected traces. Such configurations should have logarithmic size in a random incidence structure, and by the same count would cost at most a further constant multiple of \(v/k\). A linear gain would need a family of rows with disjoint selected traces whose unselected traces overlap at least threefold on average, on a linear scale. No proof or refutation of that is given here; it is recorded as a sub-idea. This paragraph is an assessment, not a claim.

Checks and scope

Control (pair-join controls). Prediction count before the run: every pair of half monomials avoiding the shared variable must reduce, for any nonzero coefficients; the two negative controls must not. Smallest nonvacuous sizes are \(h=2,3\), with joins on \(4h-1\in\{7,11\}\) variables. The exact binary computation used 68 joins of two rows meeting in one variable, with \(q\in\{5,7,11\}\), paired central, unpaired central and noncentral coefficient laws, and the shared variable in either part. All 2,796 pairs of \(h\)-subsets reduced to degree \(2h-1\). In 24 single paired rows the monomial on the \(L\)-half was irreducible, and in 24 joins through a shared selected variable the monomial on all \(2h-1\) retained \(L\)-variables was irreducible. Script and complete output: pair_join_control.py, pair_join_control.json. One earlier run stopped on an assertion because a sampled noncentral row was empty; the sampler now redraws such rows. These are checks of the lemma and its boundary, not of the asymptotic theorem.

Scope. The ceiling is for the original instance. A selected core has fewer rows and projected relations, which are not modular rows, so neither the count nor the interpolation lemma transfers; the one-way replay from cores to the original gives no upper bound on a core. Proof characteristic equal to the modulus and zero coefficients are outside the interpolation lemma.

Prior work in the record. Searches for shared, pinned, join, pair and regular ceilings returned the fractional row ceiling, the local interpolation ceiling, the all-pin fibre exclusion and the pair-parity compression. The fibre exclusion pays for conditioning and breaks even on central rows; the pair-parity compression needs globally defined pairs, whereas here a variable has a different partner in each of its nine rows. None contains (1) or (3).

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer passed the lemma, both theorems and the corollary with no mathematical error, checking every degree bound before a variable multiplication, the double count including non-integer and negative deficits and non-clean variables, and both partition probabilities. Its corrections are applied: the monomial order is stated in the proposition, existence of the example pair is justified, the facts taken from the bounded normal-form proposition are named, the generalized join condition is marked unverified with its unproved derivation cost, an unproved figure for the five-partition source is removed, and the unused hypotheses \(x\notin S\) and \(r\ge2\) are noted or dropped. Dependencies reread in full: modular row interpolation, the bounded normal-form proposition, the local interpolation ceiling and the paired source law. The record is in review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. The row-rule family is rejected by a cutoff-legal peak, and its completion by pair relations gives an actual ceiling. The mechanism still bears on the near-half statement at \(\ell=2\): the next attempt is the generalized join condition above, namely whether cycle configurations and overlapping unselected traces force a linear deficit or stop at order \(v/k\).

Sub-ideas

  • Decide whether the generalized join condition forces linear deficit on the paired source: for every set \(S\) of size \((1/2-c)v\), seek rows with nearly disjoint traces on \(S\) whose unselected traces overlap at least threefold on a linear scale, or prove by an expander-mixing or first-moment argument on the nine partitions that no such family exists. A positive answer excludes the source at \(\ell=2\); a negative one identifies the standard monomials that a proper kernel may keep.
  • Find a non-modular row type of polynomial canonical encoding whose one-pin residuals keep interpolation degree half the width, or prove that even width and half-degree interpolation always lose one degree under a single pin. Test any candidate against the accepted specification and its unbounded-witness requirement.

Process assessment. Reading the two source entries first exposed that every earlier ceiling charged one row per monomial; the mixed pair was then a short calculation, and one small exact control sufficed. 9 October 2026 — A partner swap would give the paired source a linear deficit

Conditional degree ceiling and a sharp row conjecture; the row hypothesis is unproved. Linear-deficit question for the paired source. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family, at approximation depth two the balanced paired source needs a barrier with deficit \(o(v)\). The shared-pin ceiling gives deficit of order \(v/k\) only, from rows that carry exactly half of their scope. Does the same mechanism extend to rows a constant fraction below half, which would make the deficit linear and exclude the source at depth two as well?

Route comparison. The alternatives were a normal-form construction on the monomials left by the pair rules, or this upper-bound test. The test comes first: it decides whether those monomials can be standard at all. A sharper constant in the \(v/k\) term was not pursued, since it would not change the depth-two requirement.

New mathematics. A two-step reduction is isolated. Inside a row whose trace is large, the top-degree symbol of a monomial should not change when a selected variable is exchanged for its partner, and should vanish when the trace contains a whole pair. If this holds for traces of size at least \(s_0\), a double count bounds every irreducible set and gives a ceiling with limiting deficit \(\tfrac{(r-1)(1-\theta)}{2(r+1-\theta)}v\), \(\theta=(s_0-1)/h\), for regular paired systems. The hypothesis cannot hold for \(s_0\le h-w+2\), where \(w\) is the least size of a signed zero-sum set of the row's pair weights: an explicit flat straddling the preferred cube refutes it. Whether it holds at \(s_0=h-w+3\) is a conjecture, supported by exact computation on fifteen rows and not proved.

Goal progress. Unchanged. No near-half family is produced and no unconditional exclusion is added. If the row conjecture holds, the paired source has binary PC degree at most \((1/2-0.013)v\) on its original instance and is excluded for every \(\ell\ge2\). The open statement and its required instances are as before.

General statement. thm:partner-swap-ceiling is a conditional all-parameter ceiling for regular paired central systems under a stated row hypothesis. prop:straddling-flat-sharpness proves, for every paired central row with a finite zero-sum size, that the hypothesis fails one step below the conjectured threshold. conj:paired-row-symbols is the all-parameter row statement that remains open, and cor:paired-source-conditional-exclusion is its consequence for the source.

Setting and the row hypothesis

Keep the notation of the previous entry: \(\mathcal B\), \(J_a\), \(K_E\), \(C_D\), with an odd prime modulus \(q\). In this entry the proof field has characteristic two; the row hypothesis, the proposition, the conjecture and the duality below are stated for that case only. A paired central row has scope \(X_a\) of size \(k=2h\) split into \(h\) pairs \(\{u_j,v_j\}\), nonzero weights \(a_j\), signs \(\epsilon_j\) and equation \(\sum_ja_j(x_{u_j}+\epsilon_jx_{v_j})=\tfrac12\sum_ja_j(1+\epsilon_j)\). Write \(y_j=x_{u_j}+\epsilon_jx_{v_j}-(1+\epsilon_j)/2\in\{-1,0,1\}\). The row says \(\sum_ja_jy_j=0\); a pair is preferred when \(y_j=0\), and the preferred cube \(Q_a\) is the set where all pairs are preferred. No assumption is made that a variable has the same partner in different rows.

Row hypothesis \(H(s_0)\). For every \(s\ge s_0\): (i) every monomial of degree \(s\) on \(X_a\) containing both variables of some pair has a representative of degree less than \(s\) on \(R_a\); (ii) for every pair \(\{u,v\}\) and every monomial \(m\) of degree \(s-1\) on \(X_a\setminus\{u,v\}\), the function \(x_um+x_vm\) has a representative of degree less than \(s\) on \(R_a\).

Both parts hold on the preferred cube alone, where \(x_v\) is \(x_u\) or \(1+x_u\). They say that in degrees at least \(s_0\) the graded function algebra of the row sees nothing but that cube. For \(s>h\) they follow from row interpolation.

The conditional ceiling

Consider an unsatisfiable system of paired central rows of common width \(k=2h\) with nonzero coefficients, every variable in exactly \(r\ge1\) rows, \(m=rv/k\) rows, and \(\beta\) variables that are not clean. Let \(1\le s_0\le h\), suppose all but at most \(\varepsilon m\) rows satisfy \(H(s_0)\), and put \(\theta=(s_0-1)/h\) and

\[E^*=\frac{(1-\theta)\bigl(v+(r-1)\beta\bigr)+(\theta+\varepsilon)\,rv/2}{r+1-\theta}.\tag{1}\]

Theorem (partner-swap ceiling). Under these hypotheses, if \(\lfloor E^*\rfloor+1\le v\), the canonical encoding has ordinary PC degree at most \(\max\{k,\lfloor E^*\rfloor+2\}\).

Proof. Let \(E=\lfloor E^*\rfloor+1\) and let \(S\) be an \(E\)-subset with traces \(s_a=|S\cap X_a|\). We show that \(x_S\) has a representative of degree less than \(E\) modulo \(K_E\); the derived-relation ceiling with \(w=k\), \(D=\max\{k,E+1\}\) then finishes. Suppose not. Then every \(s_a\le h\) by row interpolation. Call a row high if it satisfies \(H(s_0)\) and \(s_a\ge s_0\).

(a) A high row contains no whole pair in \(S\). Otherwise part (i) at degree \(s_a\) lowers \(x_{S\cap X_a}\) modulo \(J_a\), and multiplication by \(x_{S\setminus X_a}\) gives a relation in \(K_E\).

(b) A clean variable \(z\notin S\) has at most one high row in which its partner lies in \(S\). Let \(a\ne b\) be two such rows, with partners \(u\in S\) in row \(a\) and \(u'\in S\) in row \(b\). Cleanness gives \(X_a\cap X_b=\{z\}\), so \(u\notin X_b\). Part (ii) in row \(a\), at degree \(s_a\) with \(m=x_{(S\cap X_a)\setminus\{u\}}\), gives \(\rho\) of degree less than \(s_a\) with \(x_um+x_zm+\rho\in J_a\). Multiplying by \(x_{S\setminus X_a}\) shows \(x_S\equiv x_{S'}\) modulo \(K_E\) and lower degree, where \(S'=(S\setminus\{u\})\cup\{z\}\). Now \(S'\cap X_b=(S\cap X_b)\cup\{z\}\) has \(s_b+1\ge s_0\) elements and contains the pair \(\{z,u'\}\), so part (i) in row \(b\) lowers \(x_{S'}\) modulo \(K_E\). Thus \(x_S\) is lowered, contrary to assumption.

Count. By (a), each of the \(s_a\) variables of \(S\) in a high row \(a\) has its row-\(a\) partner outside \(S\). By (b) a clean outside variable arises this way from at most one high row, and any variable lies on at most \(r\) rows. Hence \(\Sigma:=\sum_{a\text{ high}}s_a\le(v-E)+(r-1)\beta\). A row satisfying \(H(s_0)\) that is not high has \(s_a\le s_0-1=\theta h\), and the at most \(\varepsilon m\) remaining rows have \(s_a\le h\). There are at least \(\Sigma/h\) high rows. Therefore

\[rE=\sum_as_a\le\Sigma+\theta h\,(m-\Sigma/h)+\varepsilon hm=(1-\theta)\Sigma+(\theta+\varepsilon)\frac{rv}2 .\]

Inserting the bound on \(\Sigma\) gives \(E(r+1-\theta)\le(1-\theta)(v+(r-1)\beta)+(\theta+\varepsilon)rv/2\), that is \(E\le E^*\), a contradiction. \(\square\)

For \(s_0=h\), \(\varepsilon=0\) the bound (1) is \(v/2-(r-1)(v/2-\beta)/(rh+1)\), the shared-pin ceiling; there the hypothesis is not needed, because the shared-pin drop supplies the relation of step (b) directly. For fixed \(\theta<1\) and \(\beta,\varepsilon v=o(v)\),

\[\frac{E^*}{v}\to\frac{1-\theta+r\theta/2}{r+1-\theta}=\frac12-\frac{(r-1)(1-\theta)}{2(r+1-\theta)},\]

a linear deficit. Every unit by which \(s_0\) can be lowered below \(h\) costs the source a further \((r-1)v/(2(r+1-\theta)h)\) approximately, slightly less than the first unit.

Where the hypothesis must stop

For a paired central row let \(w\) be the least size of a nonempty set \(P\) of pairs with signs \(\eta_j\in\{1,-1\}\) such that \(\sum_{j\in P}\eta_ja_j=0\), and \(w=\infty\) if there is none; equivalently the least support of a nonzero solution \(y\in\{-1,0,1\}^h\). Distinct classes \(\{a_j,-a_j\}\) give \(w\ge3\); for \(w=2\) the conjecture below would only restate row interpolation.

Proposition (straddling-flat sharpness). If \(w\le h\), then part (i) of the row hypothesis fails in degree \(s=h-w+2\). Hence \(H(s_0)\) is false for every \(s_0\le h-w+2\).

Proof. Fix \(P,\eta\) attaining \(w\) and a point \(p\in Q_a\). In a preferred pair, flipping one of its two variables gives \(y_j=1\) and flipping the other gives \(y_j=-1\). Let \(d\) be the set containing, for each \(j\in P\), the variable whose flip at \(p\) gives \(y_j=\eta_j\), and let \(d'\) be the set of their partners. Flipping all of \(d\) gives the pattern \(\eta\) on \(P\), flipping all of \(d'\) gives \(-\eta\), and flipping both returns every pair of \(P\) to a preferred state. For \(j\notin P\) flipping both variables of the pair keeps it preferred. All these flips commute, so the affine flat \(F\) through \(p\) spanned by \(d\), \(d'\) and the \(h-w\) pair flips outside \(P\) lies in \(R_a\) and has dimension \(h-w+2\).

Choose \(j_0\in P\) and let \(\mu\) be the product of both variables of pair \(j_0\) and one variable from each pair outside \(P\); it has degree \(h-w+2\) and contains a whole pair. The two variables of pair \(j_0\) lie one in \(d\) and one in \(d'\), so \(\mu\) involves one variable from each of the \(h-w+2\) spanning directions, and these directions have pairwise disjoint supports. Each of these variables takes both values along its own direction and is constant along the others, so exactly one point of \(F\) has \(\mu=1\), and the sum of \(\mu\) over \(F\) is one. In characteristic two a polynomial of degree less than \(\dim F\) sums to zero over the affine flat \(F\subseteq R_a\); hence \(\mu\) has no representative of smaller degree on \(R_a\). \(\square\)

Conjecture (paired row symbols). Let a paired central row have zero-sum size \(w\ge3\), over a field of characteristic two. Then every polynomial of degree at most \(h+w-3\) that vanishes outside \(R_a\) vanishes outside \(Q_a\). Equivalently, in every degree \(s\ge h-w+3\) the row has exactly \(\binom hs\) standard monomials, as its preferred cube does. This implies \(H(h-w+3)\).

These relations are duality. Let \(W_R(s)\) be the space of polynomials of degree at most \(2h-s\) supported on \(R_a\); in characteristic two these are the functions on \(R_a\) orthogonal, for the sum over the cube, to all polynomials of degree less than \(s\). A function on \(R_a\) has a representative of degree less than \(s\) exactly when it is orthogonal to \(W_R(s)\), and the number of standard monomials of degree \(s\) is \(\dim W_R(s)-\dim W_R(s+1)\). Since \(W_Q(s)\subseteq W_R(s)\) and \(W_R(h+1)=0\), the count statement for all \(s\ge h-w+3\) is the equality \(W_R(h-w+3)=W_Q(h-w+3)\), which is the first statement. Each function in (i) or (ii) is a function vanishing on \(Q_a\) plus a polynomial of degree \(s-1\): on \(Q_a\) one has \(x_v=x_u\) or \(x_v=1+x_u\). It is therefore orthogonal to \(W_Q(s)\), hence to \(W_R(s)\) for \(s\ge h-w+3\).

Evidence. An exact computation over the binary field on fifteen paired central rows, \(h=3,\ldots,6\), moduli from 7 to 509, compared in every degree the number of standard monomials with \(\binom hs\) and tested every instance of (i) and (ii). In all fifteen rows the set of degrees in which any of the three fails is exactly \(\{1,\ldots,h-w+2\}\), with \(w\in\{3,4\}\) or infinite; for \(w\) infinite the row is its preferred cube. The threshold \(h-w+2\) was read from the first run's level data and one worked row, then fixed and compared with all fifteen rows after \(w\) had been recomputed correctly; it is therefore a fit confirmed on the same rows, not an independent prediction. The data are small: at most 170 points, with non-preferred points at most about twice the preferred ones, whereas the source has \(|R_a|\approx2^{7h/4}\) against \(2^h\) and \(w\) of order \(h\). It is recorded in the conjecture's registry assessment and not as a separate finite-check claim: the route has registered finite checks in three of its last four research entries, so a further one would be refused. That is a limit of this record, flagged for the scheduled review; the computation is evidence for a conjecture and nothing more. Script and output: row_symbols.py, row_symbols.json. A first run used a wrong definition of \(w\) (it counted coordinate sets instead of pair sets) and is superseded; its level data were the same.

Consequence for the source

Corollary (conditional paired exclusion). Assume the paired row symbol conjecture. Then with probability \(1-o(1)\) the balanced paired source has binary PC degree at most \((1/2-0.013)v\) for large \(v\), so its original instance admits no barrier with deficit \(o(v)\) and is excluded for every \(\ell\ge2\).

Proof. Here \(h=8l\), \(q>v^2=l^24^l\ge2^{h/4}\), and the pair weights of a row are independent and uniform; conditioning on the source's good event, which has probability \(1-o(1)\), at most doubles the probabilities and expectations below. Two weights of one row fall in the same class with probability at most \(2/q\), so all rows have distinct classes except with probability \(O(mh^2/q)=o(1)\). A fixed signed set of weights sums to zero with probability \(1/q\), by conditioning on all but one weight. With \(b=0.03\), the expected number of signed sets of fewer than \(bh\) weights in one row that sum to zero is at most \(h\,2^{(H_2(b)+b)h}/q\le h\,2^{-0.025h}\), because \(H_2(0.03)+0.03<0.225\). By Markov's inequality, with probability \(1-o(1)\) at most \(\varepsilon m\) rows have \(w

Attempts to prove the row conjecture

Two attempts failed; both are recorded because they locate the difficulty.

Splitting by one pair. Let \(\omega\) be supported on \(R_a\) and orthogonal to polynomials of degree at most \(e\). The indicator of one state of a pair is a function of two variables, so it has degree at most two; multiplying test polynomials of degree at most \(e-2\) by it shows that the restriction of \(\omega\) to each state of one pair is orthogonal to polynomials of degree at most \(e-2\). For a non-preferred state this restriction is supported on a noncentral paired row on \(h-1\) pairs with target \(\mp a_j\). It vanishes if that row interpolates through degree \(e-2\). The conjecture would follow from the statement that a paired row with \(m\) pairs and target \(t\) interpolates through \(m-\lambda(t)\), where \(\lambda(t)\) is the least number of nonzero \(y_j\) with \(\sum_ja_jy_j=t\). Only \(\lambda\le1\) is known: modular row interpolation gives \(m\) for target zero and \(m-1\) for every nonzero target.

Induction on pairs. Writing a polynomial supported on such a row by the four states of one pair and comparing coefficients gives the required degree gain in every step except one: the sum of the two non-preferred restrictions is supported on the union of the rows with targets \(t-a\) and \(t+a\), and a lower bound for the degree of polynomials supported on a union of two targets is needed. Unions of targets do not obey the single-target bound in general: all targets together form the whole cube. In the range that matters, short signed relations among weights are absent and the two parts are disjoint, but disjoint supports alone do not bound the degree of a sum. No argument was found that separates the two targets without paying the degree of the separating character.

9 October 2026 — Filtration on joins of rows replaces filtration in single rows

Working ceiling and specification refinement with an unbounded witness; no near-half lower bound. Structural consequence of the shared-pin results. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family, the two preceding entries excluded one source and recorded what the bound teaches, but did not carry the mechanism into the formula specification, as this notebook's route rule requires after every theorem. Which admissibility condition does the mechanism give for arbitrary relation systems, is it non-vacuous on the accepted witness, and what does it cost?

Route comparison. Proving the paired row symbol conjecture stays the next mathematical step on this head. The specification consequence is cheap, applies to every candidate and not only to modular rows, and decides what a replacement source must satisfy; it is done first.

New mathematics. The filtered-shattering ceiling uses one row at a time. The same proof works for the join of any \(g\) rows, at the cost of a floor \(gw\): a proper cutoff kernel has a standard monomial whose trace on every such join has no lower-degree representative there. The resulting parameter \(\rho^{(g)}_F\) is at most the rowwise \(\rho_F\). On the guarded width-five witness \(\rho^{(2)}\le v-\tau\) against \(\rho_F=v-1\), a strict gap when \(\tau\ge2\) and a linear one when occurrences in \(F_N\) are bounded, yet \(\rho^{(g)}\ge(v-1)/2\) for every \(g\) below the number of clauses of one copy, so the refined condition is non-vacuous at every near-half cutoff. For the paired source \(\rho^{(2)}_{\mathbb F_2}\le v/2-(8/9-o(1))v/k\).

Goal progress. Unchanged. A necessary condition is strengthened and keeps its unbounded witness with unchanged costs. No family with a near-half barrier is produced.

General statement. thm:joint-filtration-ceiling holds for every unsatisfiable canonical Boolean relation system over every field and every \(g\ge1\). prop:joint-guarded-witness evaluates the parameter on the guarded family for all sizes, and cor:paired-joint-parameter bounds it for the balanced paired source.

The joint parameter and its ceiling

Let a canonical Boolean relation system over a proof field \(F\) have rows \(R_a\) on scopes \(X_a\) of width at most \(w\). For a set \(G\) of rows put \(U_G=\bigcup_{a\in G}X_a\) and let \(R_G\subseteq\{0,1\}^{U_G}\) be the join, the assignments satisfying every row of \(G\). Fix \(g\ge1\). Call \(S\subseteq[v]\) \(g\)-jointly filtered if for every \(G\) with \(1\le|G|\le g\) the monomial \(x_{S\cap U_G}\) has no representative of smaller degree on \(R_G\), in the Boolean algebra on \(U_G\). Let \(\rho^{(g)}_F\) be the largest size of such a set, and \(-1\) if some join of at most \(g\) rows is empty: there even the empty set fails, since one is congruent to zero. Then \(\rho^{(1)}_F\) is the local filtration parameter \(\rho_F\), and \(\rho^{(g)}_F\) is nonincreasing in \(g\). As before, an affine map from the cube on \(S\cap U_G\) into \(R_G\) that fixes those coordinates certifies the condition for \(G\), because substitution by polynomials of degree at most one does not raise the degree of a representative.

Theorem (joint filtration ceiling). For an unsatisfiable canonical Boolean relation system and every \(g\ge1\),

\[d_F\le\max\{gw,\,2,\,\rho^{(g)}_F+2\}.\tag{1}\]

Consequently a barrier through \(D\ge\max\{gw,2\}\) requires \(\rho^{(g)}_F\ge D-1\).

Proof. Suppose the degree-\(D\) closure is proper with \(D\ge\max\{gw,2\}\). By the standard-monomial part of the kernel dimension proof, reread with the filtered-shattering argument that uses it, there is a monomial \(x_S\) of degree \(D-1\) that is not congruent modulo \(C_D\) to any polynomial of smaller degree. Let \(|G|\le g\) and \(T=S\cap U_G\), and suppose \(x_T-q\) vanishes on \(R_G\) with \(\deg q\le|T|-1\). A function on \(U_G\) vanishing on \(R_G\) is a scalar combination of indicators of points \(p\notin R_G\). Such a point violates some row \(a\in G\), and its indicator is the forbidden-tuple axiom of that row at \(p|_{X_a}\) multiplied by the literals of the remaining coordinates of \(U_G\); multiplying one literal at a time reaches degree \(|U_G|\le gw\le D\). Hence \(x_T-q\in C_D\), with degree at most \(|T|\). Multiplying by the \(D-1-|T|\) variables of \(S\setminus U_G\) stays within degree \(D-1\) and gives \(x_S\equiv q\,x_{S\setminus U_G}\) modulo \(C_D\), of degree at most \(D-2\). This contradicts the choice of \(S\). So \(S\) is \(g\)-jointly filtered and \(\rho^{(g)}_F\ge D-1\). Taking \(D=\max\{gw,2,\rho^{(g)}_F+2\}\) proves (1); an empty join is refuted through \(gw\) by the same indicators. \(\square\)

For \(g=1\) this is the filtered-shattering ceiling. The floor \(gw\) is the brute-force price of the join; where a join relation has a cheaper derivation, as in the shared-pin drop, the derived-relation ceiling gives the sharper floor. The parameter depends only on finite row tables and incidences. It does not see cancellation between joins, so it is an admissibility screen and not a hardness statement.

The guarded witness

Recall the guarded family: a minimal unsatisfiable \(F_N\) on \(N\) variables with \(M\) clauses of width three or four, two disjoint copies \(x,y\), one guard \(t\), and clauses \(t\vee C(x)\), \(\neg t\vee C(y)\); \(v=2N+1\). Let \(\tau\) be the least number of variables meeting every clause of \(F_N\).

Proposition (joint guarded witness). Over every field, \(\rho^{(g)}\ge N=(v-1)/2\) for every \(g\le M-1\), and \(\rho^{(2)}\le v-\tau\). All other recorded properties of the family are unchanged.

Proof. Lower bound. Take \(S\) to be the copy \(y\). Let \(G\) have at most \(M-1\) rows. Its rows of the first kind use a proper subfamily of \(F_N\), which is satisfiable by minimality; fix a satisfying \(x^0\). The assignment \(t=0\), \(x=x^0\), \(y\) free satisfies every row of \(G\): rows of the first kind by \(x^0\), rows of the second kind by \(\neg t\). Restricted to \(U_G\) it is an affine map from the cube on \(S\cap U_G\) into \(R_G\) fixing those coordinates. Substitution along it sends a relation \(x_{S\cap U_G}-q\) with \(\deg q<|S\cap U_G|\) to a nonzero polynomial that should vanish, so no such relation exists.

Upper bound. Let \(S\) be \(2\)-jointly filtered, and take rows \(t\vee C(x)\) and \(\neg t\vee C'(y)\) with clause polynomials \(f(x),g(y)\), the indicators of the falsifying points. Both \(fg\) and \(tfg\) vanish on the join: at \(t=1\) the second row forces \(g=0\), and at \(t=0\) the first forces \(f=0\). Their top monomials are the product of all variables of \(C\) and \(C'\), and that product times \(t\). If \(S\) contained all variables of \(C\) and of \(C'\), the trace of \(S\) on the join would be one of these two monomials and would have a lower-degree representative. So for every pair \(C,C'\) the set \(S\) omits a variable of \(C\) or of \(C'\). If \(S\) contains all variables of some clause of the first copy, it omits a variable of every clause of the second copy, at least \(\tau\) variables; otherwise it omits a variable of every clause of the first copy. \(\square\)

Thus the strengthening is strict on the accepted witness whenever \(\tau\ge2\), and \(\tau\ge M/\Delta\) for maximum occurrence \(\Delta\) in \(F_N\); the record does not state a bound on \(\Delta\), so linearity of the gap is not claimed. The half \(N\ge D_v-1\) survives for every cutoff \(D_v\le v/2\). The copy \(y\) stops being filtered at \(g=M+1\): a join containing every clause of the first kind forces \(t=1\), and then the indicator of a clause of the second kind lowers the trace. Separately, in any system a join of \(g\) rows that is unsatisfiable gives \(\rho^{(g)}=-1\). Minimality of \(F_N\) is used only in the lower bound; clause widths and branching are not used.

The paired source

Corollary (paired joint parameter). With probability \(1-o(1)\) the balanced paired source has \(\rho^{(2)}_{\mathbb F_2}\le\lfloor v/2-(4v-8k^3)/(9h+1)\rfloor\), while \(\rho^{(1)}_{\mathbb F_2}=v/2\).

Proof. On the event of the shared-pin corollary, at most \(k^3\) variables fail to be clean. Its double count uses only that the set has more than \(v/2-c^*\) elements, so every set of that size or larger meets some row in more than \(h\) variables, or has two rows \(a,b\) through a clean unselected variable each meeting it in \(h\) variables. In the first case row interpolation lowers the trace on that row. In the second, apply the shared-pin drop to the set \(T_a\cup T_b\) of the two traces: the relation and its lower-degree polynomial live on \(U_G=X_a\cup X_b\), lie in the sum of the two row ideals and so vanish on the join. For the rowwise parameter, \(|L|=v/2\) in the balanced source, every trace of \(L\) is filtered by the paired retraction, and no row can carry more than \(h\). \(\square\)

A lower bound for \(\rho^{(2)}\) of the paired source is not known. The set \(L\) minus a hitting set of eight layers passes the two cases of that count, but the partner swap reduces it on a join of two rows as soon as the row hypothesis holds in the top degree, which every computed row satisfies.

Specification decision. Replace the accepted requirement \(\rho_{\mathbb F_2}\ge D_v-1\) by \(\rho^{(2)}_{\mathbb F_2}\ge D_v-1\), with width floor \(2w\le D_v\); for fixed-width families any fixed \(g\) may be used as a further screen, and the witness passes each of them for all sufficiently large \(N\) and cutoffs \(D_v\le(v+1)/2\). Keep block minimality, essential scopes, polynomial canonical encoding, occurrence and branching conditions, no common Horn polarity and consistent local binary affine consequences. The guarded family remains the unbounded witness with the same \(2N+1\) variables, width five, linear size and positive linear degree; its selected set shrinks from all non-guard coordinates to one copy. The condition is a property of pairs of row tables and incidences, with no hardness conclusion inside it. Two consequences for candidates are recorded: a modular source over an odd prime with nonzero coefficients, common even canonical row width \(k\), every variable in the same number \(r\ge2\) of rows and \(o(v)\) non-clean variables has \(\rho^{(2)}\le v/2-\Omega(v/k)\) in every proof characteristic different from the modulus, and so cannot meet the open statement's deficit \(s=o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\) for \(\ell\ge3\) when \(k=O(\log v)\); and for modular rows, two rows through an unselected variable cannot both carry disjoint traces of half their width. This decision also covers the two preceding entries, which omitted it.

Row conjecture: larger rows

Before returning to the proof of the paired row symbol conjecture, three larger rows were computed exactly with a compiled kernel, in the regime the earlier rows did not reach: the ratios of non-preferred points to the preferred cube are 4.4, 0.8 and 3.6. Here \(w\) is again the least signed zero-sum size of the pair weights, not a scope width. For \((h,q,w)=(10,211,4)\), \((10,1009,5)\) and \((12,1009,4)\) the numbers of standard monomials are \(\binom hs\) for every \(s\ge h-w+3\), and exceed it at \(s=h-w+2\): 58 against 45, 127 against 120, and 67 against 66. The conjecture survives these rows; the tested range is only the top two degrees when \(w=4\) and the top three when \(w=5\). A validation row \((5,61,3)\) agrees with the earlier script's method. These runs answer a question the fifteen small rows could not, namely whether abundant overlapping zero-sum sets create further dual polynomials above the threshold; they do not in these rows. The result is added to the conjecture's registry assessment and is not registered as a separate finite check, for the reason stated in the previous entry. Kernel and outputs: row_hilbert.c, rows.jsonl.

Scope and verification

9 October 2026 — Opposite fibres resolve, so unselected variables carry a polarity

Working general lemma and necessary conditions for arbitrary relation rows; no near-half lower bound. The shared-pin drop without modular structure. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family, the shared-pin drop was proved for modular rows, and the pairwise specification states its consequence abstractly. What is the mechanism for arbitrary relation rows, and what does it force on the unselected variables of a filtered set? This is the queued question whether some row type keeps its trace under a single pin.

Route comparison. A further proof attempt on the paired row symbol conjecture was made first and is recorded below as unsuccessful. The general mechanism was then chosen because it applies to every candidate family and tells a replacement source what its unselected variables must look like, whereas the conjecture concerns one source.

New mathematics. If the trace of one row drops on the fibre \(x=1\) and the trace of another row drops on the fibre \(x=0\), the product of the two traces drops on their join, at a cost of one degree above its own. This is the resolution rule on the variable \(x\) read on monomials. A standard monomial of a proper kernel therefore gives every unselected variable a polarity: among the rows through it with pairwise disjoint traces, either at most one trace drops on any fibre, or all traces that drop at all drop on the same single fibre. A pin-stable half-interpolating row exists, and the example is guard-like. For clause rows the statement is that the complement of the selected set meets every clause derivable by resolution within the cutoff width.

Goal progress. Unchanged. These are necessary conditions on a hypothetical barrier. No family is produced and no source is newly excluded.

General statement. lem:opposite-fibre-drop holds for arbitrary relation rows over every field. cor:fibre-polarity applies it to every standard monomial of a proper kernel, and prop:derived-clause-transversal is the corresponding statement for all clause systems and cutoffs.

The lemma

Use the notation of the shared-pin entry for an arbitrary canonical Boolean relation system of width at most \(w\) over a field \(F\): allowed sets \(R_a\), cylinder ideals \(J_a\), \(K_M=\sum_a(J_a\cap\mathcal B_{\le M})\subseteq C_{\max\{w,M\}}\).

Lemma (opposite-fibre drop). Let rows \(a\ne b\) both contain a variable \(x\), and let \(T_a\subseteq X_a\setminus\{x\}\), \(T_b\subseteq X_b\setminus\{x\}\) be disjoint. Suppose \(x_{T_a}\) has a representative \(p_a\) of degree less than \(|T_a|\) on \(R_a\cap\{x=1\}\), and \(x_{T_b}\) has a representative \(p_b\) of degree less than \(|T_b|\) on \(R_b\cap\{x=0\}\). Then for every set \(S\supseteq T_a\cup T_b\) there is \(r\) with \(\deg r<|S|\) and \(x_S-r\in K_{|S|+1}\).

Proof. Take \(p_a\) on \(X_a\setminus\{x\}\) and \(p_b\) on \(X_b\setminus\{x\}\), substituting \(x=1\), respectively \(x=0\), which does not raise degree, and put \(g_a=x_{T_a}-p_a\), \(g_b=x_{T_b}-p_b\). The function \(x\,g_a\) vanishes on \(R_a\): where \(x=0\) by its first factor, where \(x=1\) by hypothesis. So \(x\,g_a\in J_a\), and likewise \((1-x)g_b\in J_b\). Then

\[g_ag_b=g_b\cdot(x\,g_a)+g_a\cdot((1-x)g_b)\tag{1}\]

is a sum of an element of \(J_a\) and an element of \(J_b\), each of degree at most \(|T_a|+|T_b|+1\). Since the traces are disjoint, \(g_ag_b=x_{T_a\cup T_b}-r_0\) with \(\deg r_0\le|T_a|+|T_b|-1\). Multiply (1) by \(x_{S\setminus(T_a\cup T_b)}\). \(\square\)

Nothing is assumed about the rows; even \(a\ne b\) is not used. With the roles of the two fibres exchanged the same holds. The modular shared-pin drop for two rows is the case in which both traces drop on both fibres; there the derivation stays inside degree \(|S|\), here it costs \(|S|+1\), which the derived-relation ceiling allows.

Polarity of unselected variables

Let \(x_S\) be a monomial that is not congruent modulo \(C_D\) to any polynomial of smaller degree, with \(D\ge\max\{w,|S|+1\}\); for an unsatisfiable system a proper degree-\(D\) closure has such a monomial of degree \(D-1\), by the derived-relation ceiling with \(E=D-1\). For \(x\notin S\) and a row \(a\ni x\) put

\[\Delta_a(x)=\{c\in\{0,1\}:\ x_{S\cap X_a}\text{ has a representative of smaller degree on }R_a\cap\{x=c\}\}.\]

Corollary (fibre polarity). For rows \(a\ne b\) through \(x\notin S\) whose traces \(S\cap X_a\), \(S\cap X_b\) are disjoint, it is impossible that \(1\in\Delta_a(x)\) and \(0\in\Delta_b(x)\). Consequently, among rows through \(x\) with pairwise disjoint traces, either at most one has \(\Delta\ne\varnothing\), or all nonempty \(\Delta_a(x)\) are one and the same singleton.

Proof. The first statement is the lemma with \(T_a=S\cap X_a\), \(T_b=S\cap X_b\), since \(K_{|S|+1}\subseteq C_D\). For the second, let two rows \(a,b\) have nonempty sets. If \(1\in\Delta_a\) then \(0\notin\Delta_b\), so \(\Delta_b=\{1\}\), and then \(0\notin\Delta_a\) by the statement with the rows exchanged, so \(\Delta_a=\{1\}\). The case \(0\in\Delta_a\) is symmetric. \(\square\)

So for every unselected variable and every family of rows through it with pairwise disjoint traces: rows whose traces do not drop on any fibre are unconstrained, and if two or more rows drop at all they drop only on one common fibre, leaving a value \(c(x)\) at which all of them keep their traces. A \(2\)-jointly filtered set satisfies the same conclusion, because (1) vanishes on the join.

Modular rows. An even modular row with nonzero coefficients carrying half its scope has \(\Delta=\{0,1\}\) for every unselected variable, by odd-width interpolation in proof characteristic different from the modulus. The corollary then allows at most one such row through the variable among rows with disjoint traces, which is the count used in the shared-pin ceiling.

A pin-stable row. Let \(k=2h\), let \(T\) be an \(h\)-set of the \(k-1\) variables other than \(x\), let \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^{k-1}\) be the set where each of the remaining \(h-1\) coordinates equals a constant, a coordinate of \(T\) or its complement, and let \(p\) be a point. The relation \(R=(\{0\}\times Y)\cup(\{1\}\times\{p\})\) in the variables \((x,\cdot)\) interpolates through degree \(h\): a function equal to \(g\) on \(Y\), with \(g\) a polynomial in \(T\) of degree at most \(h\), and to the value \(c\) at the other point is represented by \(g+x\,(c-g(p))\). The trace \(T\) is irreducible on the fibre \(x=0\) over every field, since substituting the other coordinates by their degree-one expressions in \(T\) does not raise degree, and hence irreducible on \(R\). So a row can interpolate at half its width and keep a half trace under a pin, and then \(\Delta=\{1\}\): in this example the variable acts as a guard that releases the row at one value. This answers the queued existence question positively at the level of single rows. In a system, the rows through \(x\) with disjoint traces that drop at all must, beyond at most one, drop only on one common fibre.

Clause systems

For a clause \(E\), let \(f_E\) be the indicator of its falsifying assignment, the product of its falsified literals; its top monomial is the product of the variables of \(E\) up to sign.

Proposition (derived-clause transversal). Let an unsatisfiable CNF of width at most \(w\) have no PC refutation through degree \(D\ge\max\{w,2\}\) over \(F\). Then there is a set \(S\) of \(D-1\) variables that contains the variable set of no clause \(E\) with \(f_E\in C_D\). In particular \(S\) contains the variable set of no clause derivable from the CNF by resolution through width \(D-1\); equivalently its complement, of size \(v-D+1\), meets every such clause.

Proof. By the derived-relation ceiling with \(E=D-1\), some monomial \(x_S\) of degree \(D-1\) is not congruent modulo \(C_D\) to a polynomial of smaller degree. If \(f_E\in C_D\) and the variables of \(E\) lie in \(S\), multiply \(f_E\) by the remaining variables of \(S\) one at a time; degrees stay at most \(D-1\), and \(x_S\) becomes congruent to a polynomial of smaller degree. For the second statement, input clauses have \(f_E\in C_w\). If \(E_1=x\vee A\) and \(E_2=\neg x\vee B\) have a non-tautological resolvent \(A\vee B\) of width at most \(D-1\), then

\[f_{A\vee B}=f_{B\setminus A}\,f_{E_1}+f_{A\setminus B}\,f_{E_2},\]

because \(f_{E_1}=(1-x)f_A\) and \(f_{E_2}=x\,f_B\) up to the sign convention of the literal. Both products are reached by multiplying by one literal at a time and have degree at most \(|A\cup B|+1\le D\). A weakening \(E\vee\ell\) has \(f_{E\vee\ell}=f_\ell f_E\), one more literal. Induction over a derivation in which every derived clause has width at most \(D-1\) gives \(f_E\in C_D\) for each of its clauses; input clauses of width \(D\) may be used as premises. \(\square\)

For clause rows the sets of the corollary are explicit. For \(x\notin S\) and a clause \(x^{\sigma}\vee A\), the trace drops on a fibre exactly when that fibre falsifies the literal of \(x\) and every variable of \(A\) lies in \(S\). When \(A\) and \(B\) have disjoint variable sets, the polarity statement says that two such clauses with opposite literals of \(x\) cannot both have their other variables inside \(S\). For clauses sharing literals the same conclusion follows from the proposition's identity, and the proposition extends it to all derivations within the cutoff.

Specification decision. No change to the accepted requirement \(\rho^{(2)}_{\mathbb F_2}\ge D_v-1\). The fibre polarity is a consequence of it and is recorded as a screening test for candidates: for every variable outside the selected set, the rows through it with pairwise disjoint traces whose traces drop on some fibre must, beyond at most one row, all drop on one common fibre only. The derived-clause transversal at near-half width is not adopted as a specification condition. It is necessary for a barrier, but it fails as soon as the empty clause is derivable in width \(D_v-1\), so it contains a resolution-width lower bound, a global hardness statement and not a property of row tables and incidences; the guarded witness is not known to satisfy it at near-half width. It is kept as a necessary test for any proposed barrier proof, not as a property of the envelope.

The row conjecture: a third attempt

A peeling argument was tried on the paired row symbol conjecture. The following is an unverified sketch, not a result. If, for some pair, both non-preferred restrictions of a polynomial supported on a shifted row vanished, the polynomial would factor through \(1+\pi\) for that pair and an induction on the number of pairs could proceed. The restrictions would vanish by degree only when the pair lies in no short representation of the target. Heuristically, when signed zero-sum sets are abundant, as in the source, a given pair lies in about \(2h/w\) zero-sum sets of size \(w+1\), which together involve all pairs, so no such pair is available at the first step. At best the sketch could handle rows with isolated zero-sum sets, which is not the source's regime; nothing is claimed. The obstruction remains a degree bound for polynomials supported on two shifted rows at once.

Scope and verification

Scope. The lemma is a sufficient condition for a drop; the clause example shows it is strictly stronger than adding drops fibre by fibre, since one drop on each of the two opposite fibres suffices. The proof uses disjoint traces; they are not always necessary, as clause rows sharing literals show. Nothing here bounds a degree from below.

Prior work in the record. Searches for resolvents, transversals of derivable clauses and fibre polarity returned only the filtered-shattering ceiling and the shared-pin drop. That polynomial calculus simulates resolution with one extra degree is standard; the proposition only combines it with the standard monomial.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer confirmed the lemma, its identity, the corollary's deduction and the resolvent identity, and required corrections that are applied: the proposition and the standard-monomial step now assume unsatisfiability and cite the derived-relation ceiling; the pin-stable example uses coordinates that are constants, selected coordinates or their complements, so that irreducibility holds over every field; every restatement of the polarity carries the disjoint-trace hypothesis and no longer suggests that rows without a drop are constrained; the clause paragraph separates the disjoint case from the general one; weakening is treated; the third attempt is marked as an unverified sketch. Unused hypothesis noted: the two rows need not be distinct. Dependencies reread in full: local derivability, the derived-relation ceiling and the joint filtration entry. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing, with rotation at the four-entry boundary. The spell produced an unconditional ceiling, a conditional linear ceiling, a refined specification and this general lemma, but no proof, reduction or refutation that advances the near-half statement itself, so no extension is claimed. The row conjecture stays queued under this item.

The queued existence question for pin-stable rows (the second sub-idea of the shared-pin entry) is answered by the explicit relation above; it stays in the queue under this item until an entry develops it in turn.

Process assessment. The general lemma was found by asking what the modular drop uses; it uses only that two fibres reduce, and one fibre each suffices. The conjecture attempt cost the first part of the cycle and ended at the obstruction already named. The required specification paragraph was written before the checkpoint this time because turn start printed it.
