9 October 2026 — Measure the cutoff against the kernel's own monomials, not against all variables

Working alternative sufficient endpoint and goal-level review; whether any family can meet it is unknown. Review of the near-half line after six research entries. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. Six more research entries leave both open statements open, and every source examined loses at least order \(v/\log v\) below half. This is the scheduled goal-level review. Is a barrier within \(o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\) of half of all variables really what the source theorem needs, or is it an artefact of how the contraction rate is estimated?

New mathematics. The contraction engine uses the number of variables only through a lower bound for a ratio of error ranks. Those ranks count standard monomials of a down-closed family contained in the standard monomials of the old closure. The Kruskal–Katona theorem bounds the ratio by the size of that family's levels: if the old closure has at most \(\binom Xj\) standard monomials in the degrees just below the cutoff \(K\), with \(X\) at most about \((2+1/\delta)(K-\delta)\), the ratio at shift \(\delta\) is at least \(1/(1+e\delta)\). With this rate the moving-cutoff source theorem holds at every fixed depth, with polylogarithmic approximation degrees, for any cutoff \(D\ge v^{1/2}\). For a CNF it suffices that the sets of the relevant sizes containing no clause scope number at most \(\binom Xj\). This is an alternative sufficient endpoint, not a weakening of the near-half one: when the top levels are full cubes on \(X\) variables it asks for a barrier within \(O(X/\Delta)\) of \(X/2\), and nothing shows that a thin closure can be proper.

Goal progress. Unchanged. thm:thin-kernel-source-exclusion adds a second sufficient endpoint to the first open statement, which thereby becomes a disjunction: near half of all variables, or a proper closure that is thin just below its cutoff. The two are incomparable as stated. Nothing shows that thin and proper are jointly satisfiable; the only compatibility check is the lower bound \(\binom{D-1}{j}\) on level sizes. In the cube case the new endpoint is again a near-half statement, with a smaller allowed deficit. An additional sufficient condition of unknown attainability is a larger toolbox, not a change in what must be proved. The complete Frege transfer is untouched.

General statement. lem:kruskal-katona-growth holds for every Boolean polynomial system, cutoff and prefactor over the binary field. thm:thin-kernel-source-exclusion is the source theorem for all fixed depths and inventory exponents under the thin-kernel hypothesis, and cor:scope-free-thinness gives a sufficient condition for all CNF families.

Across the goal

  • Near-half Boolean PC family. Open. All six research entries since the last review took it as primary: the pairing criterion, the balanced paired source, the shared-pin ceiling, the conditional partner-swap ceiling, the joint filtration specification and the opposite-fibre lemma. They produced one repaired source, its exclusion for \(\ell\ge3\), a conditional exclusion for \(\ell=2\), and two refinements of necessary conditions. None produced a proper kernel near half. Six cycles were spent on this statement, and the open-item count is two, as it was twelve research entries back.
  • Complete Frege transfer. Open. No entry took it as primary; zero cycles. It is unaffected by this review except that its old family may now have any cutoff \(D\ge v^{1/2}\), so its width and encoding ledger is no longer tied to half the variables.

Obstacle

The line is stuck on one implication: an unsatisfiable polynomial-size Boolean family whose degree-\(D\) closure is proper at a \(D\) so large that the error ranks of the contraction engine stop growing just below \(D\). With the ambient estimate this means \(D\) within \(o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\) of \(v/2\). Every mechanism that makes rows interpolate exactly at half their width, modular parity above all, loses a degree as soon as two rows meet in an unselected variable, and the loss is of order \(v/k\) at width \(k\); known lower-bound technology reaches about a quarter. The obstacle is therefore the normalization by the full variable count, together with the absence of any lower-bound method that reaches a constant fraction of a ceiling.

Architecture review

Necessary target. The weakest endpoint identified so far is sufficient and not shown necessary. For each fixed \(\ell\ge2\) and inventory exponent \(A\): a polynomial-size unsatisfiable Boolean family with old system \(\Gamma_v\), a cutoff \(D\) with \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma_v)\), and a cutoff \(K=D-\lceil v^{1/3}\rceil\) at which every error rank function of the engine satisfies \(c_P(K-\delta)/c_P(K)\ge1/\operatorname{polylog}(v)\) for the polylogarithmic shifts \(\delta\) that occur. Nothing else about \(v\) enters the source theorem.

Extra requirements. The current approach demands more in three places. It bounds the ratio by the ambient binomial ratio, which forces \(K\) near \(v/2\); the engine only needs the ratio for down-closed subfamilies of the old standard monomials. It asks for a ratio tending to one; a ratio \(1/(1+\delta)\) suffices at fixed depth, because degrees then grow by squaring and stay polylogarithmic. And it has sought sources whose rows interpolate exactly at half width, which is what the shared-pin mechanism punishes. The first two demands are replaced below by a condition on level sizes. Whether that makes the third unnecessary depends on a thin proper closure existing, which is open.

Independent alternative. Before seeing this route, the review's medium reviewer received only the goal, the engine's two inequalities and the proved negative results. It answered that the near-half requirement is not needed as stated, since the source theorem uses it only through the second inequality, "a plateau condition on the rank functions", and proposed three architectures: averaging over cutoffs under a small pseudo-quotient, re-filtering the algebra by defined extension variables, and a constant-loss comparison with the Hilbert function of the base quotient. The first is empty: a proper degree-\(D\) closure has quotient dimension at least \(2^{D-1}\) by the recorded kernel dimension lemma, which is the falsifier the reviewer named; this bounds the rank from which contraction starts, not every individual error rank. The third compared cumulative deficits of the base Hilbert function; the lemma below gives a proved bound in terms of level sizes instead. The second is kept as a sub-idea. The stage-one record is in independent-review.txt.

Rank normalization. This is the point of the review. Losses and survivors are already measured in one quotient, but the rate was normalized by the ambient cube. The error rank \(c_P(k)\) is the number of standard monomials of degree at most \(k\) of the error kernel, a down-closed family inside the standard monomials of \(C_D\). The recorded counterexample shows that the ratio of the base quotient's Hilbert function cannot replace the ambient ratio. Its level sizes can: Kruskal–Katona bounds every down-closed subfamily by the size of the top levels of the family containing it. So the Kruskal–Katona dimension \(X\) of the old quotient's top levels can take the role of \(v\), as an alternative sufficient condition. It does not relax the barrier relative to that dimension: the cutoff must still be near \(X/2\).

Decision. Add the thin-kernel endpoint to the first open statement as an alternative: a proper closure at a cutoff within \(O(X/\Delta)\) of half the Kruskal–Katona dimension \(X\) of its standard monomials near that cutoff. It is not a special or general case of the near-half statement. Test its attainability before any specification change; the accepted specification stays as it is. Retain the pairwise filtration condition as a necessary screen. Stop repairing modular sources toward exact half of all variables; the paired row symbol conjecture stays queued.

Decisive test. Next cycle, decide whether thin and proper are compatible away from the cube case. The claim to prove or refute: if the standard monomials of \(C_D\) number at most \(\binom Xj\) in the degrees just below \(K\), then \(1\in C_D\) once \(D\ge X/2+c\) for an absolute constant \(c\), by an interpolation argument on the standard family in place of the cube. If it holds, the endpoint needs a barrier within \(O(X/\Delta)\) of the interpolation ceiling of the effective dimension and is no easier than near-half; the route then returns to the old endpoint and to the extension-variable filtration. If a thin family with a ceiling well above \(X/2\) exists, test bounded-width random CNF at near-threshold density, where thinness sets in at \(c^*(k,\Delta)v\) (\(0.341v\) at \((3,4.27)\)) against a scope-free ceiling near \(0.54v\). Unchecked pointer from the reviewer: resolution width upper bounds for random \(k\)-CNF fall like \(v/\Delta^{1/(k-2)}\) while \(c^*\) falls like \(\Delta^{-1/k}\), so large densities are likely to fail.

Error ranks count a down-closed family

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with a Boolean system \(\Gamma\) containing the Boolean axioms, \(C_D=C_D(\Gamma)\), and multilinear representatives. Fix a degree-compatible monomial order. For a prefactor \(P\) of degree at most \(a\) and inputs \(g_i\) of degree at most \(d\), with \(a+d+K\le D\), put \(\ker_k=\{f\in V_k:\ Pg_if\in C_D\text{ for all }i\}\) for \(k\le K\), so that the engine's rank is \(c_P(k)=\dim V_k/\ker_k\) as recorded. A weight multiplying the prefactor is covered by counting its degree in \(a\); iterated prefactors of the engine fit the hypothesis through its ceiling \(K+\Delta_j+\Delta_{j-1}\le D\).

(a) \(\ker_k=\ker_K\cap V_k\), by definition. (b) If \(f\in\ker_k\) and \(k<K\), then \(xf\in\ker_{k+1}\) for every variable \(x\): the polynomial \(Pg_if\in C_D\) has degree at most \(a+d+k\le D-1\), so its product with \(x\) lies in \(C_D\). (c) \(\ker_k\supseteq C_D\cap V_k\), by the same absorption. Let \(\mathfrak M_P\) be the set of monomials of degree at most \(K\) that are not leading monomials of elements of \(\ker_K\). By (a), a leading monomial of degree \(j\) is the leading monomial of an element of \(\ker_j\); by (b), if \(m\) is such a monomial and \(x\nmid m\), then \(xm\) is the leading monomial of the multilinear form of \(xf\), because the other terms become \(xm'\) with \(m'\prec m\) or keep a smaller degree. So leading monomials are closed under multiplication by a new variable within degree \(K\), and \(\mathfrak M_P\) is down-closed. Counting dimensions, \(c_P(k)\) is the number of elements of \(\mathfrak M_P\) of degree at most \(k\). By (c), \(\mathfrak M_P\subseteq\mathfrak M_0\), the standard monomials of \(C_D\) of degree at most \(K\). Write \(m_j(\cdot)\) for the number of monomials of degree exactly \(j\).

Lemma (Kruskal–Katona growth). Let \(1\le\delta\le K\) and let \(X\ge K\) be real with \(m_j(\mathfrak M_0)\le\binom Xj\) for every \(K-\delta<j\le K\). Then for every prefactor \(P\) and inputs as above,

\[\frac{c_P(K-\delta)}{c_P(K)}\ \ge\ \Bigl(1+\sum_{i=1}^{\delta}\rho^i\Bigr)^{-1},\qquad \rho=\frac{X-K+\delta}{K-\delta+1}.\tag{1}\]

In particular \(X\le2(K-\delta)+1\) gives \(c_P(K-\delta)/c_P(K)\ge1/(1+\delta)\), and \(\rho\le1+1/\delta\), that is \(X\le2(K-\delta)+1+(K-\delta+1)/\delta\), gives at least \(1/(1+e\delta)\), since \(\sum_{i\le\delta}\rho^i\le\delta(1+1/\delta)^\delta\). The input degree \(d\) enters only through \(a+d+K\le D\); \(\delta\) is independent of it. Here \(\binom Xj=X(X-1)\cdots(X-j+1)/j!\).

Proof. Let \(\mathfrak M=\mathfrak M_P\) with level sizes \(m_j\le m_j(\mathfrak M_0)\). Fix \(j\) in the window with \(m_j>0\) and write \(m_j=\binom{x}{j}\) with real \(x\ge j\); then \(x\le X\), since \(\binom{\cdot}{j}\) is increasing on \([j-1,\infty)\). By the Lovász form of the Kruskal–Katona theorem the shadow of a family of \(\binom xj\) sets of size \(j\) has at least \(\binom x{j-1}\) sets, and a down-closed family contains the shadows of its levels. Iterating, \(m_i\ge\binom xi\) for \(i\le j\). With \(i=K-\delta\),

\[\frac{m_j}{m_{K-\delta}}\le\frac{\binom xj}{\binom x{K-\delta}}=\prod_{t=K-\delta}^{j-1}\frac{x-t}{t+1}\le\rho^{\,j-K+\delta},\]

because each factor is at most \((X-K+\delta)/(K-\delta+1)\). Summing over the window, \(c_P(K)-c_P(K-\delta)\le m_{K-\delta}\sum_{i=1}^\delta\rho^i\), and \(m_{K-\delta}\le c_P(K-\delta)\). \(\square\)

For \(X=v\) the lemma is weaker than the ambient bound, whose ratio tends to one: it compares with the single level \(m_{K-\delta}\) and never exceeds about \(1/(1+\delta)\). This loss is harmless only because the shifts stay polylogarithmic. The recorded three-variable counterexample has level sizes \(1,2,1\) for the error family and \(1,3,1\) for the base; with \(K=2,\delta=1,X=2\) the bound is \(2/3\) against the actual \(3/4\), so the lemma is consistent with it while the ratio of base Hilbert functions, \(4/5\), is not a valid bound.

The source theorem with a thin kernel

Theorem (thin-kernel source exclusion). Fix \(\ell\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), \(A>0\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/(3\ell)\). Let \(\Gamma_v\subseteq\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]\) contain the Boolean axioms, let \(D=D(v)\ge v^{1/2}\) with \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma_v)\), and put \(K=D-\lceil v^{1/3}\rceil\). There is a constant \(c=c(\ell,r,A)\) such that, with \(\Delta=\lceil(\log v)^{c}\rceil\), the following holds for large \(v\). Put \(X=2(K-\Delta)+1+(K-\Delta+1)/\Delta\). If the standard monomials of \(C_D(\Gamma_v)\), for some degree-compatible order, number at most \(\binom{X}{j}\) in every degree \(K-\Delta<j\le K\), then the system obtained from \(\Gamma_v\) by adding at most \(v^A\) complete binary ENS blocks in levels \(1,\ldots,\ell\) of accuracy \(h=\lfloor v^\epsilon\rfloor\), with the product-only grammar and input degree \(r\) of the moving-cutoff theorem, has no PC refutation through degree \(\lfloor v^{1/3}\rfloor\).

Proof. Follow the proof of the moving-cutoff theorem, reread in full, with one change. It uses the engine's rate only as a number \(\eta\) with \(c_{P'}(K)\le c_P(K)-\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\le(1-\eta)c_P(K)\) for inputs of degree \(d\). Take \(\eta(d)=\tfrac1{2(1+ed)}\), valid by the lemma for every shift \(d\le\Delta\): the window for \(\Delta\) contains that for \(d\), and \(\rho_d=(X-K+d)/(K-d+1)\le1+1/d\) because \((1+1/d)(K-d+1)-(X-K+d)=2(\Delta-d)+(K-d+1)/d-(K-\Delta+1)/\Delta\ge0\). Set \(\Delta_0=r\), \(t_j=\lceil2(1+e\Delta_{j-1})\log(2\ell(v^A+1))\rceil\), \(\Delta_j=\Delta_{j-1}t_j\). Then \(\Delta_j\le(C\log v)^{2^j-1}(r+1)^{2^j}\) for a constant \(C=C(\ell,A)\), so all \(\Delta_j\) are at most \(\Delta\) for suitable \(c\), and \(M(1-\eta(\Delta_{j-1}))^{t_j}\le M\exp(-t_j\eta)\le\tfrac1{2\ell(M+1)}M\) for every inventory \(M\le v^A\); the \(\ell\) error terms sum to less than one half. The numbers \(t_j\) are polylogarithmic, hence at most \(h\); the reserve \(K+C'\Delta_\ell\le D\) holds because \(\Delta_\ell\) is polylogarithmic and \(D-K=\lceil v^{1/3}\rceil\); helper degrees are \(O(h^\ell)=o(v^{1/3})\) as before; and \(K\ge2\Delta-1\), hence \(X\ge K\) as the lemma requires, since \(D\ge v^{1/2}\); a cutoff \(D\ge v^{1/3}+\operatorname{polylog}v\) would do. Unsatisfiability of \(\Gamma_v\) is not used, as in the original theorem. The coefficient selection, the single common multiplier and the replay of a supposed refutation are unchanged, since they use only these numerical facts and the kernel \(C_D\). \(\square\)

The cube case. If the top levels are those of a full cube on \(X'\) effective variables, the hypothesis reads \(X'\le X\), that is \(K\ge X'/2-O(X'/\Delta)\). Interpolation on those variables bounds the degree by \(X'/2+O(1)\). So there the theorem is a near-half statement in the effective dimension with allowed deficit \(O(X'/\Delta)\), where \(\Delta\) is a power of \(\log v\) growing with \(\ell\): a narrower window than the moving-cutoff theorem's \(o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\). The theorem does not subsume that theorem. It can be easier only for families whose top levels are sparse without being concentrated on about \(2K\) variables, and none is known to have a proper closure.

The hypothesis is about the closure and is not a property that can be read from a formula. The next statement gives one that can.

Corollary (scope-free thinness). Let \(\Gamma_v\) be the canonical polynomial form of a CNF. If the number of \(j\)-sets of variables containing the variable set of no clause is at most \(\binom{X}{j}\) for \(K-\Delta<j\le K\), with \(X\) as in the theorem, the thinness hypothesis holds. The same is true with the sets that are \(g\)-jointly filtered for some \(g\) with \(g\cdot\text{width}\le D\), or the sets avoiding every clause derivable by resolution in width \(K\), in place of scope-free sets.

Proof. A monomial whose variable set contains a clause scope is the leading monomial of a multiple of that clause's indicator, of the same degree, which lies in \(C_D\). So standard monomials are scope-free. For the other two families use the joint filtration argument and the derived-clause computation: in each case a monomial outside the family is congruent modulo \(C_D\) to a polynomial of smaller degree, hence is a leading monomial. \(\square\)

Calibration. For \(m=\Delta v\) uniformly random \(k\)-clauses the expected number of \(cv\)-sets containing no scope is at most \(2^{v(H_2(c)-\Delta c^k\log_2e+o(1))}\) (the exact exponent has \(\Delta\log_2(1-c^k)\)), and by Markov's inequality with a union bound over the window sizes the actual numbers are at most \(v\) times that with probability \(1-\Delta_{\mathrm{win}}/v\), \(\Delta_{\mathrm{win}}\) the window length. Against \(\binom{2cv}{cv}=2^{2cv-o(v)}\), thinness holds for every \(c\) with \(H_2(c)-\Delta c^k\log_2e<2c\) strictly; \(c^*\) denotes the least grid point with this property, a conservative value. Numerically \(c^*=0.341,0.275,0.164\) for \(k=3\) and \(\Delta=4.27,10,50\); \(0.356\) and \(0.256\) for \(k=4\), \(\Delta=9.93,50\); \(0.370\) for \((5,21.1)\); \(0.393\) for \((7,87.8)\); \(0.414\) for \((10,708)\) (evaluation). So for dense bounded-width formulas this sufficient condition is met at a constant fraction of \(v\) below one half, falling with density. For clause width \(\kappa\log v\) at threshold density \(c^*\to1/2\), which is the ambient case again. Its scope-free ceiling at \((3,4.27)\) is near \(0.54v\) by the same first moment, so the endpoint would ask for a degree lower bound at about \(0.63\) of that ceiling, beyond the recorded technology, and the true ceiling may be lower.

Falsification attempt on this line

The line's general claim was that some source with rows interpolating at half their width has a proper kernel near half of all variables. The shared-pin ceiling refutes it for regular even modular sources at \(\ell\ge3\), and the opposite-fibre lemma shows the loss is the resolution rule and not a modular accident. Against the new endpoint three attacks were tried. A proper closure has a standard monomial of degree \(D-1\) with all its subsets standard, so level \(j\) has at least \(\binom{D-1}{j}\) monomials; this is compatible with the bound \(\binom{2(K-\Delta)+1}{j}\) and does not refute the endpoint. The quotient-growth counterexample is consistent with the lemma. And the reviewer's small-quotient variant is refuted by the kernel dimension lemma. A fourth attack succeeds in part: in the cube case the hypothesis is a near-half condition on the effective variables with a smaller allowed deficit, and with the exact form \(X\le2(K-\Delta)+1\) it would be empty there, which is why the theorem carries the slack \((K-\Delta+1)/\Delta\). Outside the cube case the endpoint is neither refuted nor shown attainable.

Outside leads

  • Kruskal–Katona, Lovász form (Lovász, Combinatorial Problems and Exercises, Problem 13.31): a family of \(\binom xj\) sets of size \(j\) has shadow at least \(\binom x{j-1}\). Target: the near-half statement, through the engine's growth ratio. It would break if error ranks were not counts of a down-closed family. Answers. It removes the normalization by the full variable count, which is the obstacle: the cutoff is compared with the dimension of the old quotient's own top levels. Test. Passed: the down-closure is proved above, the lemma is proved, and it agrees with the recorded three-variable counterexample (\(2/3\le3/4\)).
  • Knapsack degree bound (Impagliazzo–Pudlák–Sgall, Lower bounds for the polynomial calculus and the Gröbner basis algorithm, the subset-sum degree theorem in characteristic zero). Target: a mechanism that reaches half of the variables. It would break on Boolean encodings in characteristic two. Answers. It is the one classical bound at half the variable count, so it would supply the missing hard family if it survived a polynomial-size Boolean encoding. Test. Not run: the recorded shared-pin ceiling concerns regular even modular rows under the old normalization and is not a test of knapsack encodings or of the thin endpoint; carry encodings, whose auxiliary variables enter the count, were not examined.
  • Expansion degree bound (Ben-Sasson–Impagliazzo and Alekhnovich–Razborov: degree at least half the boundary expansion of medium row sets). Target: a lower bound reaching the thinness threshold. It would break if boundaries are too small. Answers. It is the available lower-bound method, and the new endpoint asks only for a constant fraction of the ceiling. Test. Falsified at near-threshold densities, by an estimate and not a computation: a set of rows has boundary at most the number of variables covered exactly once, heuristically at most about \(v/e\) for random scopes, so the method gives at most about \(0.184v\), below \(c^*v\) for the tabulated pairs other than \((3,50)\), which was not estimated. It is not falsified as a method for other row structures.

Absurd bridges

  • Frozen variables in random constraint satisfaction (Achlioptas–Coja-Oghlan, Algorithmic barriers from phase transitions): in the clustered phase most variables are frozen within a cluster. Translation: frozen variables correspond to monomials removed from the standard family, free ones to its Kruskal–Katona dimension; a theorem there would say dense formulas have few free directions. Smallest test: count scope-free sets of a random \(k\)-CNF. Answers. It names where thin kernels come from, namely dense local constraints, which is what the obstacle needs once the normalization is intrinsic. Test. Not run: the scope-free count above tests the calibration, not this translation; no frozen-variable or cluster statement was used, and the tabulated densities are at or above the satisfiability threshold.
  • Vanishing ideals of small point sets and Reed–Muller erasure decoding (Kudekar–Kumar–Mondelli–Pfister–Şaşoğlu–Urbanke, Reed–Muller codes achieve capacity on erasure channels). Translation: read the old quotient as functions on a set of pseudo-solutions; a set of \(N\) points has at most \(N\) standard monomials in total, so it is thin at every level \(j\) with \(N\le\binom{X}{j}\). A theorem there would give thin kernels from formulas whose relaxation has few solutions and a low-degree-generated vanishing ideal, with one further constraint that is hard to see. Smallest test: the level bound for a point set. Answers. It gives a construction principle for the thin endpoint that does not go through half of the variables. Test. Passed for the level bound only, which is immediate and does not use the cited theorem. The construction itself, a relaxation with at most \(\binom{X}{K}\) solutions whose closure is its full vanishing ideal and an extra constraint not refutable through \(D\), is not attempted.

Checks, scope and verification

Scope. The theorem is over the binary field, as is the moving-cutoff theorem it modifies. It assumes the old closure is proper and thin; it produces neither. The corollary's condition is sufficient, not necessary. The calibration is a first-moment bound for random clause sets and makes no claim about their PC degree.

Unused hypotheses: unsatisfiability in the theorem, and \(D\ge v^{1/2}\) beyond \(K\ge2\Delta-1\). 9 October 2026 — Linear consequences do not count as variables; the half ceiling for thin kernels stays undecided

Working proofs of two normalizations; the architecture test is undecided and one sentence of the review is corrected. Architecture test after the thin-kernel review. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the review asked whether a thin closure can be proper above half its Kruskal–Katona dimension \(X\): prove or refute that level sizes at most \(\binom Xj\) force \(1\in C_D\) for \(D\ge X/2+c\). The missing implication is a family meeting either endpoint; the test decides whether the thin endpoint is anything other than near-half in another normalization. A proof ends the thin route; a polynomial-size counterexample would be a candidate.

Architecture test. Outcome of the decisive test named in the thin-kernel review: undecided. No proof was found, and the counterexample attempted does not work. The attempt also shows that the review's sentence "interpolation on those variables bounds the degree by \(X'/2+O(1)\)" is not supported in general: the record contains half ceilings only for particular sources (modular rows, the paired source, random relation rows), not for every unsatisfiable Boolean system. That sentence, and the same assertion in the stage-one brief given to the reviewer, are corrected here. What stands: in the cube case the thin hypothesis requires \(K\ge X'/2-O(X'/\Delta)\). A proper closure at such a cutoff is excluded only for sources with a recorded half ceiling; for other systems it is open.

New mathematics. Two normalizations. Affine axioms over \(\mathbb F_2\) can be substituted away without changing the refutation degree, and the moving-cutoff theorem then applies to the substituted system, so its variable count is the free dimension \(n=v-r\) and not \(v\). And if the closure contains, through degree \(K\), the vanishing ideal of a set of \(N\) points, it has at most \(N\) standard monomials of degree at most \(K\), while a proper closure has at least \(\sum_{i\le K}\binom{D-1}{i}\); so the thin endpoint is available only when \(\log_2N\) is at least about \(D-1\) and is met when it is at most about \(2K\).

Goal progress. Unchanged. The first lemma lets the open statement count free dimensions, which is a weaker sufficient target, but no family is supplied and, as with the moving cutoff itself, a weaker sufficient convenience is not a necessary implication proved. The architecture test did not decide the thin endpoint.

General statement. lem:affine-free-dimension holds for every Boolean polynomial system over \(\mathbb F_2\) containing consistent affine axioms and every cutoff at least two and at least the axiom degrees. lem:point-count-thinness holds for every Boolean system, point set and cutoff.

Affine axioms can be substituted away

Lemma (affine free dimension). Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]\) contain the Boolean axioms and affine polynomials whose span \(\Lambda\) has dimension \(\varrho\) and does not contain \(1\). After Gaussian elimination write the zero set of \(\Lambda\) as \(z_i=\alpha_i(y)+c_i\), \(1\le i\le\varrho\), with \(y\) the remaining \(n=v-\varrho\) variables and \(\alpha_i\) linear. Let \(\sigma\) be the substitution homomorphism and \(\Gamma^\sigma=\sigma(\Gamma)\) together with the Boolean axioms of \(y\). Then for every \(D\ge2\) at least the degrees of the elements of \(\Gamma\):

  1. \(1\in C_D(\Gamma)\) if and only if \(1\in C_D(\Gamma^\sigma)\).
  2. For any further set \(E\) of polynomials, possibly in additional variables which \(\sigma\) fixes, a PC refutation of \(\Gamma\cup E\) of degree \(B\ge2\) gives one of \(\Gamma^\sigma\cup\sigma(E)\) of degree at most \(B\).

Proof. For 2 apply \(\sigma\) to every line. It is a ring homomorphism that does not raise degree. Elements of \(\Lambda\) go to zero. A Boolean axiom \(z_i^2-z_i\) goes to \((\alpha_i+c_i)^2-(\alpha_i+c_i)=\sum_{j}(y_j^2-y_j)\) over the support of \(\alpha_i\), in characteristic two, a combination of Boolean axioms of \(y\). A multiplication by \(z_i\) becomes multiplication by \(\alpha_i+c_i\), a combination of multiplications by variables and a scalar, at the same degree. Other axioms go to elements of \(\Gamma^\sigma\cup\sigma(E)\). This also gives the forward direction of 1. Conversely, for \(g\in\Gamma\) of degree \(e\le D\), \(g-\sigma(g)\) lies in the ideal of the polynomials \(z_i-\alpha_i-c_i\in\Lambda\) with cofactors of degree at most \(e-1\), replacing one \(z_i\) at a time; so \(\sigma(g)\in C_D(\Gamma)\). The Boolean axioms of \(y\) are in \(\Gamma\). Hence \(C_D(\Gamma^\sigma)\subseteq C_D(\Gamma)\). \(\square\)

The bound \(D\ge\) axiom degrees is used only in the converse of 1, and \(D,B\ge2\) only to admit the Boolean axioms of \(y\).

Consequence for the source theorem. The moving-cutoff theorem takes any polynomial set with the Boolean axioms. Apply it to \(\Gamma^\sigma\) on \(n\) variables: if \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma)\) for \(D=\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\), \(s=o(n/(\log n)^{\ell-2})\), then by the converse direction of 1, which needs \(D\) at least the axiom degrees, the hypothesis holds for \(\Gamma^\sigma\). The theorem, with all its parameters taken in \(n\) (accuracy \(h=\lfloor n^\epsilon\rfloor\), at most \(n^A\) blocks, large \(n\)), says the augmented system over \(\Gamma^\sigma\) has no refutation through degree \(\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\), and by 2 neither has the augmented system over \(\Gamma\) with the same blocks. Here \(\sigma\) of a block is the block on the substituted inputs: a complete binary ENS block consists of fresh coefficient variables, their domain equations and the formal product and companions, all polynomial expressions in the inputs and the fresh variables, as the main notebook's block definition states. Inputs keep their degree bound, and the product-only grammar is untouched. A bound of \(v^{A'}\) blocks is covered when \(v\le n^{C}\). So the first open statement may be read with \(n=v-\varrho\) in place of \(v\), provided accuracy, block count and proof degree are also expressed in \(n\); with \(v\le n^C\) this changes exponents by constant factors only, which the transfer statement must carry. The substituted system need not be a CNF or have bounded width; the theorem does not ask for that, but the Frege transfer statement does and is not touched here.

Relation to the record. The main notebook's residual-coordinates lemma is this elimination for label bits of one base (lem:residual-coordinates-linear-elimination, summary read; not relied on). The thin-kernel count gives the same normalization with a worse window: variables that are leading monomials of affine elements of \(C_D\) are not standard, so level \(j\) has at most \(\binom{n}{j}\) standard monomials. The substitution argument is stronger and makes the Kruskal–Katona route unnecessary for this case.

What it admits. Bounded-width systems in which most variables are parities of a small free set: after substitution the rows are bounded-arity relations on linear forms, hence wide in the free variables. The recorded row ceilings were proved for rows on their own variables and count every variable. For this class a standard monomial may be taken inside any basis of the free variables, and a row constrains it only through the basis variables it contains. Whether shared-pin, polarity or interpolation ceilings in the free dimension follow is not examined in this entry.

Point counts bound the thin endpoint from both sides

Lemma (point-count thinness). Let \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma)\) for an unsatisfiable Boolean system over a field with axioms of degree at most \(D\), \(D\ge2\), and let \(W\subseteq\{0,1\}^v\) have \(N\) points with \(I(W)\cap V_K\subseteq C_D\) for some \(K\le D\). Then the standard monomials of \(C_D\) of degree at most \(K\), for a degree-compatible order, number at most \(N\) and at least \(\sum_{i\le K}\binom{D-1}{i}\).

Proof. Standard monomials of degree at most \(K\) are linearly independent modulo \(C_D\cap V_K\supseteq I(W)\cap V_K\), so they are independent as functions on \(W\). For the lower bound, the kernel dimension theorem gives a set of \(D-1\) variables all of whose subsets are standard. \(\square\)

The upper bound uses neither unsatisfiability nor properness; the lower bound does not use \(W\).

So the thin hypothesis \(m_j\le\binom Xj\) holds for all \(j\) in the window as soon as \(N\le\binom{X}{K-\Delta+1}\), roughly \(\log_2N\le2K\), provided \(\binom Xj\) is non-decreasing on the window, that is \(X\ge2K-\Delta+1\), which holds once \(K\ge\Delta^2+\Delta-1\), and no \(W\) with \(\log_2N\) much below \(D\) exists. In these terms the thin endpoint asks for a barrier at half the number of bits of a relaxation whose low-degree vanishing ideal is derivable, where the barrier can never exceed that number of bits. For one-hot blocks the candidate count alone gives little: \(B\) blocks of \(b\ge3\) variables with exactly one true have at most \(\binom Bj(b-1)^j\) standard monomials at level \(j\), and this bound is below \(\binom{2j}{j}\) only for \(j\ge0.77B\) at \(b=3\), for \(j\ge0.92B\) at \(b=4\), and at no level for \(b\ge5\) (solve \(H_2(\kappa)+\kappa\log_2(b-1)\le2\kappa\)). It is an upper bound on the level sizes, so this does not exclude such encodings.

The attempted counterexample

Take a partition of the cube \(\{0,1\}^n\) into \(R_1,R_2\) with \(|R_2|\) odd, axioms all polynomials of degree at most \(D=n-1\) vanishing on \(R_1\) or on \(R_2\). Every decomposition \(1=f_1+f_2\) has \(f_1\) equal to the indicator of \(R_2\), of degree \(n\), so the static sum \(I(R_1)_{\le D}+I(R_2)_{\le D}\) omits \(1\). But this sum is \(\{f\in V_D:\sum_{\alpha\in R_2}f(\alpha)=0\}\), and it is closed under the legal multiplications if and only if for each variable \(x\) the indicator of \(R_2\cap\{x=1\}\) is a multiple of that of \(R_2\) plus an affine function, since functionals on \(V_{n-2}\) given by sums over sets are determined modulo affine indicators. An affine function supported in a face is zero or the face, so in each direction some face is contained in or disjoint from \(R_2\); for \(n\ge2\) this forces \(R_2\) or \(R_1\) to be a single point, and then the system is satisfiable. Otherwise the hyperplane is not closed and the closure is all of \(V_D\). So this construction fails definitively, as the reviewer completed the argument. It tests only \(D=n-1\). No unsatisfiable example with a proper closure above \(n/2+O(1)\) and axioms within the cutoff is recorded, and no general ceiling either; the proposed ceiling is neither refuted nor proved, also in the cube case.

Specification decision. Following the rule recorded today in Where we stand, the weakened target is matched by a weakened specification. Adopted: rows may include affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\); with \(\varrho\) the rank of the affine rows present in the encoding, not of derivable affine consequences, the variable count in the cutoff is the free dimension \(n=v-\varrho\), with \(D_n=\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\), \(v\le n^{C}\), and the pairwise filtration condition reads \(\rho^{(2)}_{\mathbb F_2}\ge D_n-1\), computed on the original rows including the affine ones. The branching-density condition \(\liminf h/v\ge1/(2w)\) was derived by counting all variables and is required only when \(\varrho=0\); for \(\varrho>0\) it is withdrawn until re-derived in the free dimension. Polynomial canonical encoding, no common Horn polarity, consistent local affine consequences, a structural requirement not derived from the variable count, and \(2w\le D_n\) are unchanged. Witness: the guarded width-five family has no affine rows, so \(\varrho=0\), and satisfies the old specification, hence the weakened one, with the same paid parameters; no new witness is required for a relaxation. The thin-kernel alternative is not adopted into the specification, because its attainability is undecided.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer found no error in either proof and required corrections that are applied: the point-count lemma states the axiom degree bound and the monotonicity condition for its window; the one-hot remark is corrected for \(b\ge4\) and weakened to a statement about the candidate count; the source-theorem consequence states its parameters in the free dimension, cites the block definition and separates the affine rank from the input-degree bound; the counterexample's failure is completed to a definitive one; the specification decision fixes the rank as that of affine rows present and where the filtration is computed. The reviewer knew no general half ceiling over \(\mathbb F_2\) and no example beating it. Unused hypotheses are noted after each lemma. Dependencies reread in full: the moving-cutoff entry, the ENS block definition, the kernel dimension entry, the thin-kernel review. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. No queue item is developed in this entry; it performs the review's architecture test, which the turn guidance requires first.

9 October 2026 — Rows on dense parities pass every local screen near half

Working proofs for parity-defined rows; local conditions only, no degree lower bound. Research cycle on the free-dimension class. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the free-dimension count admits bounded-width systems whose variables are parities of \(n\) free variables. The earlier sources failed at a local level: two rows through an unselected variable already cost a deficit of order \(v/k\). Does that deficit persist in the free dimension, or do such systems escape the local ceilings? A persistent deficit ends the class; an escape moves the whole difficulty to the global closure and says what a candidate must then be tested against.

New mathematics. A row that is a relation on linear forms constrains a monomial in the free variables only through forms of its span supported inside the monomial. Hence if every nonzero combination of the forms of any \(g\) rows has weight above \(E\), every set of at most \(E\) free variables is filtered on every join of \(g\) rows, also in the bounded-width chain encoding. Random dense forms give \(E=n/2-O(\sqrt{ngk\log v})\) for all \(g\) simultaneously up to almost linear size, so the shared-pin deficit and every recorded join screen disappear in this class.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The result is about necessary local conditions. It supplies no proper closure: the systems it covers may well be refutable far below half, and a heuristic dimension count for random instances suggests a sublinear degree at fixed \(k\) and less than \(n/3\) at logarithmic \(k\).

General statement. lem:parity-trace-criterion holds over every field of characteristic two for every nonempty preimage of a relation under a linear map over \(\mathbb F_2\). prop:dense-parity-local-filtration holds for every system of parity-defined rows and every \(g\), with an explicit random existence statement.

Setting

Free variables \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\). A parity-defined row \(a\) consists of \(k\) linear forms \(\ell_{a,1},\ldots,\ell_{a,k}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) and a relation \(R_a\subseteq\{0,1\}^k\); it allows the set \(A_a=\{y:(\ell_{a,i}(y))_i\in R_a\}\). The chain encoding has, for each form, partial-sum variables with width-three affine rows \(s_j=s_{j-1}+y_{i_j}\), and the canonical clauses of \(R_a\) on the final sums. Its affine rows have rank equal to the number of auxiliary variables, so its free dimension is \(n\), and by the affine free dimension lemma its refutation degree at any cutoff at least \(\max\{k,2\}\) is that of the substituted system \(\Gamma^\sigma\) in the \(y\) alone, whose axioms are the clause polynomials of the \(R_a\) evaluated at the forms. Over \(\mathbb F_2\) these generate the truncated ideals \(I(A_a)\cap V_D\) inside the closure at every such cutoff: a linear change of coordinates preserves degree, and a function vanishing on \(A_a\) is \(\sum_m m\,g_m(\ell)\) with \(m\) monomials in complementary coordinates and each \(g_m\) a combination of the degree-at-most-\(k\) clause polynomials. The proposition below does not use this identification.

What a parity row can see

Lemma (parity trace criterion). Let \(M:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^t\) be linear with row space \(\Lambda\), let \(R\subseteq\mathbb F_2^t\) and let \(U=M^{-1}(R)\) be nonempty. Let \(T\) be a set of coordinates such that no nonzero form of \(\Lambda\) is supported inside \(T\). Then over a field of characteristic two no polynomial of degree less than \(|T|\) agrees with \(y_T=\prod_{i\in T}y_i\) on \(U\).

Proof. Take \(u\in U\); then \(u+\ker M\subseteq U\). The projection \(\pi_T:\ker M\to\mathbb F_2^T\) is onto: otherwise a nonzero linear functional on \(\mathbb F_2^T\) vanishes on \(\pi_T(\ker M)\), which is a nonzero form supported in \(T\) lying in \((\ker M)^\perp=\Lambda\). Choose a subspace \(H\subseteq\ker M\) mapped isomorphically onto \(\mathbb F_2^T\). On \(u+H\) the \(T\)-coordinates range over all of \(\{0,1\}^T\), and every other coordinate is an affine form over \(\mathbb F_2\) in them, hence in characteristic two an affine polynomial in them. Suppose \(p\) has degree less than \(|T|\) and equals \(y_T\) on \(U\). Substituting those affine polynomials, \(p\) restricts to a polynomial of degree less than \(|T|\) in the \(T\)-coordinates that equals \(y_T\) on \(\{0,1\}^T\), contradicting uniqueness of multilinear representatives. \(\square\)

Characteristic two is used: over other fields a parity of Boolean coordinates is not an affine polynomial.

The criterion is sufficient and is not claimed to be necessary.

Proposition (dense parity local filtration). Work in characteristic two. Let a system of parity-defined rows with every \(R_a\) nonempty have the property that every nontrivial \(\mathbb F_2\)-combination (coefficients not all zero) of the forms of any \(g\) rows has weight greater than \(E\), for some \(E\ge0\). Then:

  1. the forms of any \(g\) rows are independent, and their rows are jointly satisfiable;
  2. for every set \(T\) of at most \(E\) free variables and every \(g\) rows, \(y_T\) has no lower-degree representative on \(\bigcap A_a\) over those rows;
  3. in the chain encoding, for any \(g\) clause rows together with any affine rows, with \(U\) the set of variables of these rows, \(y_{T\cap U}\) has no lower-degree representative on their join, for the same \(T\).

If the \(mk\) forms are independent uniform elements of \(\mathbb F_2^n\), the hypothesis holds with \(E_g=\lceil n/2-\sqrt{ngk\ln(2mk)}\rceil-1\) simultaneously for all \(g\ge1\) with \(E_g\ge0\), with probability at least \(1-\sum_{g\ge1}(2mk)^{-gk}\).

Proof. 1. A dependency is a nonzero combination of weight zero. Independent forms make the stacked map onto \(\mathbb F_2^{gk}\), so the preimage of the nonempty product relation is nonempty. 2. Apply the lemma to the stacked map and the product relation. 3. A representative on the join is a polynomial in the join's variables of degree less than \(|T\cap U|\) equal to \(y_{T\cap U}\) at every assignment satisfying the listed rows. Every \(y\in\bigcap A_a\) extends, by the values of all partial sums, to such an assignment. Substituting the affine expressions of the auxiliary variables in the \(y\) does not raise degree and gives a representative of \(y_{T\cap U}\) on \(\bigcap A_a\), contradicting 2 applied to \(T\cap U\). For the random statement, a fixed nonempty subset of independent uniform forms has a uniform sum, whose weight is below \(n/2-\lambda\) with probability at most \(e^{-2\lambda^2/n}\). The subsets inside some \(g\) rows number at most \(m^g2^{gk}\le(2mk)^{gk}\); with \(\lambda=\sqrt{ngk\ln(2mk)}\) the union bound gives \((2mk)^{gk}e^{-2gk\ln(2mk)}=(2mk)^{-gk}\). \(\square\)

Reading. In the chain encoding the pairwise-filtered parameter satisfies \(\rho^{(2)}\ge n/2-O(\sqrt{nk\log(mk)})\), and likewise \(\rho^{(g)}\) for every \(g\) with \(gk\log(mk)=o(n/(\log n)^{2\ell-4})\), within the deficit the goal allows. The shared-pin drop, the fibre polarity and the joint filtration ceiling at these \(g\) therefore give no bound below about \(n/2\) for a set of free variables. Each of those results remains true. One-row fibre lowering does occur: on the fibre \(s_2=c\) of a first chain row, \(y_{i_1}y_{i_2}=(1+c)y_{i_1}\). What does not occur for sets of at most \(E\) free variables is the two-sided hypothesis, a second row through the same auxiliary variable with a disjoint trace lowered on the opposite fibre: the next chain row has a trace of at most one free variable, and part 3 excludes the conclusion. The shared-pin statement itself was not in the reviewer's excerpts; this reading of it is mine. In the earlier sources the local deficit came from full rows meeting in single variables; here free variables are shared by many chains, but no clause row sees them except through long parities.

What this does not give. The filtered sets are sets of free variables; nothing is claimed for monomials containing auxiliary variables, which is harmless for a lower bound, since one standard monomial suffices, but means the proposition is a statement about a screen and not an identification of the closure. Passing every local screen up to almost linear \(g\) is necessary for a barrier near \(n/2\) and far from sufficient. For independent random rows a dimension count is discouraging. With one forbidden tuple per row, unsatisfiability needs about \(m\ge2^kn\ln2\) clause rows; the degree-\(D\) multiples of one row number about \(\binom n{D-k}\) against \(\binom nD\) monomials; and if the multiples are as independent as their number allows, the unit is reached where \(((n-D)/D)^k\approx m\), near \(D\approx n/(1+2n^{1/k})\). For fixed \(k\) this is \(\Theta(n^{1-1/k})\), sublinear; for \(k=c\log_2n\), the largest width with polynomial size, it is a constant fraction strictly below \(n/3\). This is a heuristic count of the kind made for semi-regular systems, not a proved ceiling. A candidate in this class therefore needs forms and relations with many syzygies among the row multiples, as the knapsack has, and the test for it is the recorded global one: an odd-mass function agreeing on each forbidden set with a polynomial of degree at most \(n-D-1\).

Specification decision. No condition is added or removed. Recorded for the weakened specification adopted in the preceding entry: with affine rows its pairwise filtration condition is met at deficit \(s\ge\sqrt{2nk\ln(2mk)}+1\) by every system satisfying the weight hypothesis for \(g=2\), so in this class that condition is not binding; sparse-parity systems can still fail it. The random dense-parity family above, with \(v=n+O(mkn)\) variables, width \(\max\{3,k\}\) and free dimension \(n\), is an unbounded witness of this one condition only: unsatisfiability, absence of a common Horn polarity, consistent local affine consequences and \(2w\le D_n\) are not checked for it here. A global condition that would discriminate, such as the absence of a low-degree partition identity for the forbidden sets, is not adopted: it has no proof of necessity beyond the definition of the closure and no witness.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer found the lemma and the three parts sound after repairs that are applied: the hypothesis speaks of nontrivial combinations with \(E\ge0\) and nonempty relations throughout; part 3 uses the trace on the join's variables; the random statement uses \(E_g\); the setting names the substituted system and adds the argument identifying the truncated row ideals; a false sentence about pins of auxiliary variables is replaced; the heuristic is stated as sublinear at fixed width and below \(n/3\) at logarithmic width; the specification paragraph no longer overclaims. Unused hypotheses: \(gk\le n\), dropped; bounded \(k\). Not verifiable from the reviewer's excerpts: the shared-pin statement, reread here. Dependencies reread in full: the free-dimension entry, the joint filtration entry, the opposite-fibre entry, the shared-pin entry. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. No queue item is developed; this entry carries out the next step named by the preceding entry, a sub-idea of the review now queued.

Sub-ideas

  • Prove or refute the dimension-count ceiling for random parity-defined clause rows: a degree upper bound of about \(n/(1+2n^{1/k})\), by showing the row multiples have no more syzygies than the Koszul ones through that degree.
  • Construct structured forms and relations in this class with a global obstruction: an odd-mass function whose restriction to each forbidden set has degree at most \(n-D-1\) with \(D\) near \(n/2\); start from the knapsack's symmetric functions with parities of blocks in place of single variables.
  • Extend the parity trace criterion to monomials containing auxiliary variables and to odd characteristic, if a use arises.

Two cycles after the review the picture is clearer than the review left it: the thin-kernel alternative is undecided and not needed for the useful part, the free-dimension count is the real weakening, and in the class it opens the local screens that occupied the previous block are vacuous. The search now has to be for global structure, which the record has so far approached only through the static unit test.

9 October 2026 — The engine needs few free extensions of a standard monomial, not few variables

Working proofs of a local form of the growth bound and its source theorem; no family is shown to meet it. Research cycle on global structure for the free-dimension class. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the preceding entry left the search for global structure. Before choosing a family, what exactly must the old closure provide for the contraction engine? The thin-kernel theorem asked for small global counts of standard monomials. Is there a condition on the closure that can be read from what a partial assignment forces, so that structured candidates can be tested against it? A local condition would name the property to design for; if none is weaker than a global count, the search stays with near half of the free dimension.

New mathematics. The growth of the engine's error ranks is bounded by the number of ways a standard monomial extends to a standard monomial one degree higher. If every standard monomial of degree \(j-1\) just below the cutoff has at most \((1+1/\Delta)j\) such extensions, the ranks contract at rate \(1/(2(1+ed))\) and the source theorem holds, by a double count that needs neither the Kruskal–Katona theorem nor any bound on the number of variables or of standard monomials. A variable is not an extension of \(x_S\) whenever the closure forces it on the face \(x_S=1\). So a sufficient form of the endpoint reads: once about \(K\) variables are set to one along a standard monomial, all but about \(K\) of the remaining variables are forced.

Goal progress. Unchanged. This is a further sufficient endpoint. It contains the cube and free-dimension cases only in the narrower window \(O(v/\Delta)\) of the thin-kernel theorem, and does not subsume the moving-cutoff theorem. As conditions on abstract down-closed families it neither implies thin counts nor follows from them. No family with a proper closure is shown to satisfy it outside those cases.

General statement. lem:extension-count-growth holds for every Boolean system over \(\mathbb F_2\), cutoff and prefactor. thm:forced-extension-source-exclusion is the source theorem for all fixed depths and inventory exponents under the extension-count hypothesis.

Extension counts bound the growth

Keep the notation of the thin-kernel review: \(\Gamma\) Boolean over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(C_D\) its closure, a degree-compatible order, \(\mathfrak M_0\) the standard monomials of \(C_D\) of degree at most \(K\), and for a prefactor \(P\) of degree at most \(a\) and inputs of degree at most \(d\) with \(a+d+K\le D\) the down-closed family \(\mathfrak M_P\subseteq\mathfrak M_0\) of multilinear monomials whose numbers of elements of degree at most \(k\) are the engine's ranks \(c_P(k)\), as proved there. For a standard multilinear monomial \(x_S\) of degree less than \(K\) let its extension count be

\[e(S)=\#\{x\notin S:\ x\,x_S\in\mathfrak M_0\}.\]

Lemma (extension count growth). Let \(1\le\delta\le K\) and suppose \(e(S)\le\varepsilon_j\) for every standard \(x_S\) of degree \(j-1\), for each \(K-\delta<j\le K\). Then for every prefactor and inputs as above, with \(m_j\) the number of elements of \(\mathfrak M_P\) of degree \(j\),

\[m_j\le\frac{\varepsilon_j}{j}\,m_{j-1},\qquad c_P(K)\le\Bigl(1+\sum_{i=1}^{\delta}\prod_{t=1}^{i}\frac{\varepsilon_{K-\delta+t}}{K-\delta+t}\Bigr)c_P(K-\delta).\tag{1}\]

In particular \(\varepsilon_j\le(1+1/\delta)j\) on the window gives \(c_P(K)\le(1+e\delta)c_P(K-\delta)\). Nothing in the lemma is specific to \(\mathbb F_2\) beyond the setting in which the family \(\mathfrak M_P\) was constructed.

Proof. Count pairs \((g,f)\) with \(f\in\mathfrak M_P\) of degree \(j\), \(g\) of degree \(j-1\) and \(g\mid f\). Each \(f\) has exactly \(j\) divisors of degree \(j-1\), all in \(\mathfrak M_P\) since it is down-closed. Each \(g=x_S\in\mathfrak M_P\subseteq\mathfrak M_0\) lies below at most \(e(S)\le\varepsilon_j\) elements of \(\mathfrak M_0\) of degree \(j\), hence below at most that many of \(\mathfrak M_P\). So \(j\,m_j\le\varepsilon_j\,m_{j-1}\). Iterating from \(K-\delta\), \(m_{K-\delta+i}\le m_{K-\delta}\prod_{t\le i}\varepsilon_{K-\delta+t}/(K-\delta+t)\); sum over \(i\) and use \(m_{K-\delta}\le c_P(K-\delta)\). With \(\varepsilon_j\le(1+1/\delta)j\) each product is at most \((1+1/\delta)^\delta\le e\). \(\square\)

For the cube on \(X\) variables \(e(S)=X-|S|\), and (1) implies the bound of the Kruskal–Katona growth lemma with \(\rho=(X-K+\delta)/(K-\delta+1)\), its factors being at most \(\rho\); the earlier lemma needed only the level sizes, this one only the local counts. For abstract down-closed families neither hypothesis implies the other: a thin family can have one monomial with many extensions, and bounded extension counts near the cutoff do not bound level sizes by binomial coefficients. Neither example is shown to arise as the standard monomials of a closure.

Theorem (forced extension source exclusion). Fix \(\ell\ge2\), input degree \(r\ge1\), \(A>0\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/(3\ell)\). Let \(\Gamma_v\subseteq\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]\) contain the Boolean axioms, let \(D\ge v^{1/2}\) with \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma_v)\), \(K=D-\lceil v^{1/3}\rceil\), and \(\Delta=\lceil(\log v)^c\rceil\) with the constant \(c=c(\ell,r,A)\) of the thin-kernel theorem. If, for some degree-compatible order, every standard multilinear monomial \(x_S\) of \(C_D\) with \(K-\Delta\le|S|<K\) has \(e(S)\le(1+1/\Delta)(|S|+1)\), then the product-only ENS source over \(\Gamma_v\) with at most \(v^A\) blocks in \(\ell\) levels of accuracy \(\lfloor v^\epsilon\rfloor\) has no PC refutation through degree \(\lfloor v^{1/3}\rfloor\), for large \(v\).

Proof. For a shift \(d\le\Delta\) the window of \(d\) lies in that of \(\Delta\), and \((1+1/\Delta)j\le(1+1/d)j\). So the lemma gives the rate \(\eta(d)=1/(2(1+ed))\) used in the proof of the thin-kernel theorem, whose recursion \(t_j=\lceil2(1+e\Delta_{j-1})\log(2\ell(v^A+1))\rceil\), \(\Delta_j=\Delta_{j-1}t_j\), error ledger, reserve and replay use the rate only as that number, as does the moving-cutoff proof it follows, reread for this entry. The condition \(X\ge K\) there served only the Kruskal–Katona lemma and has no counterpart. The hypotheses \(1\notin C_D\), \(D\ge v^{1/2}\) and \(\epsilon<1/(3\ell)\) are inherited and not used in the new step. \(\square\)

Forcing

A variable \(x\notin S\) is not an extension of a standard \(x_S\) as soon as \(x\,x_S\) is congruent modulo \(C_D\) to a polynomial of degree at most \(|S|\), since it is then a leading monomial. This holds in particular when \((x+c)\,x_S\in C_D\) for a constant \(c\): the closure forces \(x=c\) on the face where the variables of \(S\) are one. Forcing is monotone: \((x+c)x_T\in C_D\) gives \((x+c)x_S\in C_D\) for \(S\supseteq T\) while \(|S|+1\le K\le D\). So \(e(S)\) is at most the number of variables outside \(S\) not forced in this degree-preserving sense, and the theorem's hypothesis is implied by:

for every standard \(x_S\) with \(K-\Delta\le|S|<K\), all but at most \((1+1/\Delta)(|S|+1)\) of the variables outside \(S\) satisfy \(x\,x_S\in C_D+V_{|S|}\).

Cases. In the cube nothing is forced and the condition is \(v-|S|\le(1+1/\Delta)(|S|+1)\), near half of all variables with deficit \(O(v/\Delta)\). With affine axioms of rank \(\varrho\), take an order in which each eliminated variable is the largest variable of its reduced form. Then it is a leading monomial, and so is every multiple of it within the cutoff, so it is never an extension; this bounds \(e(S)\) directly by the order and not through the displayed condition, since \(x\,x_S\) is congruent to a polynomial of degree \(|S|+1\). The hypothesis is then near half of the free dimension. With nonlinear definitions the count can drop further in a way the free-dimension count does not see: if \(z+y_1y_2\) is an axiom, then \(z\,y_1y_2\equiv y_1y_2\) and \(z\,y_1\equiv z\), so \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) are forced by \(\{z\}\): setting a product variable to one forces its factors. The converse forcing of \(z\) by \(\{y_1,y_2\}\) is true but plays no role, because \(y_1y_2\) is the leading monomial of the axiom and no standard monomial contains both. For an unsatisfiable system with axioms of degree at most \(D\), the kernel dimension theorem supplies a standard monomial of degree \(D-1\) with all subsets standard, which gives \(e(S)\ge D-|S|-1\) for its subsets, which is compatible with the condition.

What this does not give. Only all-ones faces along standard monomials are used. Whether the condition may be applied after complementing some variables depends on the source theorem's grammar being invariant under that change, which is not checked here. The condition is sufficient and concerns the closure, which is not known for any candidate. Forcing many variables makes refutation easier as well: the same implications that reduce extension counts shorten derivations, and nothing here shows that a closure with few extensions can be proper at the required cutoff. As with thin counts, the allowed window in the cube case, \(O(v/\Delta)\), is narrower than the moving-cutoff theorem's.

Specification decision. No change. The rule recorded in Where we stand applies only when the target is weakened by a statement known to be attainable beyond the old cases; this endpoint, like the thin-kernel one, is an alternative of unknown attainability. Considered and not adopted: a specification clause "variables defined as products of others are admitted and not counted". It would follow from the forcing condition only for particular closures, and it has no witness with a proper closure. Recorded as the property to test on the first structured candidate.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer passed the lemma, its display and the theorem's reduction, found no hidden use of level sizes, and required corrections that are applied: the goal-progress paragraph no longer says the endpoint contains the near-half statement; the affine case is stated as a consequence of the order and not of the forcing condition; the vacuous half of the product example is marked; monotonicity of forcing, the source of the top standard monomial and the scope of the comparison with the Kruskal–Katona lemma are stated; the unjustified remark on complemented coordinates is replaced; the display is written without a quotient. Dependencies reread in full: the thin-kernel review, the moving-cutoff entry, the kernel dimension entry. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. No queue item is developed; the entry continues the next step named by the preceding entry.

9 October 2026 — On the product-tree cube the engine's cutoff is two fifths of the leaves and the ceiling is one half

Working proofs for one explicit frame; no contradiction with a proper closure at the cutoff is found. Research cycle testing the extension-count condition. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the extension-count theorem asks that standard monomials just below the cutoff have few standard extensions. Test it on one explicit structure, the cube on \(n\) free variables extended by product variables along a binary tree: what are the standard monomials, at which cutoff does the condition hold for every system containing this structure, and how far is that cutoff from the degree at which every such system is refutable? A cutoff above the ceiling would end this frame; a window names what a contradiction must achieve.

New mathematics. For \(n=2^h\) leaves, the standard monomials of the product-tree definitions are the antichains of tree nodes containing no two siblings, one for each subset of leaves, with degree the number of maximal dyadic blocks of the subset; the top degree is \(n/2\). An antichain of size \(s\) has at most \(\max\{0,2(n-2s)-1\}\) extensions. Hence for every system containing the frame the extension-count condition holds once \(K-\Delta\ge(2n+4)/5\), and every unsatisfiable such system with further axioms of degree at most \(w\) is refuted in degree \(n/2+w\). The engine's requirement is a barrier at about \(0.4n\) where the trivial ceiling is \(0.5n\), on \(2n-1\) variables.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The frame gives an explicit window, not a family: no contradiction over the frame is shown to keep its closure proper at \(0.4n\). In this filtration the expected degree of a standard monomial is \(0.36n\), below the cutoff by a linear margin, so the requirement is at least as demanding as degree \(n/2\) on the plain cube, where the cutoff sits at the mean.

General statement. prop:product-tree-frame holds for every \(n=2^h\) over \(\mathbb F_2\). cor:product-tree-cutoff holds for every Boolean system over \(\mathbb F_2\) containing the frame.

The frame

Let \(n=2^h\ge2\). The nodes \(u\) of the complete binary tree of height \(h\) carry variables \(z_u\); the leaves are the free variables. Write \(L_u\) for the set of leaves below \(u\). The frame \(\Pi_n\) has the Boolean axioms and

\[z_u+z_{u0}z_{u1}\ \ (u\text{ internal with children }u0,u1),\qquad z_uz_w+z_u\ \ (w\text{ a proper descendant of }u).\]

It has \(2n-1\) variables, \(O(n\log n)\) axioms of degree two, and its zero set \(W\) is the set of \(2^n\) assignments of the leaves with every \(z_u\) the product of the leaves in \(L_u\). On \(W\) a monomial \(\prod_{u\in A}z_u\) is the function \(y_T=\prod_{i\in T}y_i\) with \(T=\bigcup_{u\in A}L_u\).

Proposition (product tree frame). For every degree-compatible order and every \(D\ge2\):

  1. The standard monomials of \(C_D(\Pi_n)\) of degree at most \(D\) are exactly the monomials \(z_A\) of degree at most \(D\) with \(A\) an antichain of nodes containing no two siblings. Each subset \(T\) of leaves corresponds to exactly one such \(A\), the set of maximal \(L_u\subseteq T\), and \(C_D(\Pi_n)\cap V_j=I(W)\cap V_j\) for \(j\le D\).
  2. For \(D\ge n/2\) the largest degree of a standard monomial is \(n/2\), and the normal form of a uniformly random \(T\) has expected degree \(n\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}2^{-i}2^{-2^i}(1-2^{-2^i})+2^{-n}\), which is \(0.3589\,n\) up to \(o(1)\). No concentration is claimed.
  3. For a sibling-free antichain \(A\) of size \(s\), the number of nodes \(x\) with \(A\cup\{x\}\) a sibling-free antichain is at most \(\max\{0,2(n-2s)-1\}\).

Proof. 1. The rewriting rules \(z_w^2\to z_w\), \(z_{u0}z_{u1}\to z_u\), \(z_uz_w\to z_u\) lower the degree, and each is an axiom, so applying one to a monomial of degree \(j\le D\) changes it by an element of \(C_D\) of degree at most \(j\). Their left sides are therefore leading monomials for any degree-compatible order, as are their multiples within degree \(D\). A monomial to which no rule applies is squarefree with support an antichain without siblings. Such an \(A\) is determined by \(T=\bigcup L_u\). The maximal blocks of any \(T\) form a sibling-free antichain and partition \(T\). Each \(u\in A\) is a maximal block of \(T\): if the parent's leaves lay in \(T\), the sibling's leaves would be covered by elements of \(A\), which cannot be the sibling itself, as \(A\) is sibling-free, nor lie above it, as they would be comparable to \(u\); so they lie strictly below it, and a cover of a dyadic block by proper sub-blocks forming an antichain contains two siblings. Since the maximal blocks partition \(T\) and \(A\) covers \(T\), \(A\) is all of them. Distinct \(T\) give linearly independent functions \(y_T\) on \(W\). So every polynomial of degree at most \(j\le D\) is congruent modulo \(C_D\cap V_j\) to a combination of normal forms of degree at most \(j\), which vanishes on \(W\) only if it is zero. This gives \(C_D\cap V_j=I(W)\cap V_j\). A normal form \(z_A\) is standard: an element of \(C_D\) with leading monomial \(z_A\) would, after reducing its other monomials, which only lowers their degree or keeps them normal and never produces \(z_A\) from a different monomial of the same degree, be a nonzero combination of normal forms vanishing on \(W\). So normal forms are exactly the standard monomials. 2. A set meeting each sibling pair of leaves in exactly one leaf has \(n/2\) maximal blocks. Conversely map each element of a sibling-free antichain to a sibling pair of leaves: its own pair if it is a leaf, any pair below it otherwise. Two leaves of one pair are siblings, a leaf and an internal node above its pair are comparable, and two incomparable internal nodes have disjoint leaf sets; so the map is injective and the size is at most \(n/2\). For the expectation, a non-root node at height \(i\) is a maximal block of \(T\) with probability \(2^{-2^i}(1-2^{-2^i})\), there are \(n2^{-i}\) such nodes, and the root contributes \(2^{-n}\). 3. Each element of \(A\) blocks at least two leaves from being added or lying below an added node: a leaf blocks itself and its sibling, an internal node the leaves below it. These blocked sets are disjoint for different elements. So at most \(n-2s\) leaves can be added. An internal node that can be added has no element of \(A\) below it and no leaf below it that is the sibling of a leaf of \(A\), since it would then lie above that leaf of \(A\); so all leaves below it are addable, and the addable internal nodes are internal nodes of a forest on at most \(n-2s\) leaves, at most \(n-2s-1\) of them when \(n>2s\). \(\square\)

Part 3 is close to sharp: for \(A\) one leaf from each of the first \(s\) pairs, all nodes inside the remaining \(n-2s\) leaves can be added, at least \(2(n-2s)-2\log_2n-2\) of them.

Corollary (product tree cutoff). Let \(\Gamma\supseteq\Pi_n\) be a Boolean system over \(\mathbb F_2\) in the variables of the frame, with further axioms of degree at most \(w\). Unsatisfiable means that these have no common zero on \(W\), the Boolean zero set of the frame.

  1. If \(\Gamma\) is unsatisfiable, then \(1\in C_D(\Gamma)\) for \(D=n/2+w\).
  2. For every \(D\) and every standard monomial \(z_A\) of \(C_D(\Gamma)\), the extension count is at most \(\max\{0,2(n-2|A|)-1\}\). Hence the hypothesis of the forced extension source theorem holds for \(\Gamma\) whenever \(1\notin C_D(\Gamma)\), \(D\ge v^{1/2}\) with \(v=2n-1\), and \(K-\Delta\ge(2n+4)/5\).

Proof. 1. Unsatisfiability gives functions \(g_a\) on \(W\) with \(\sum_ag_af_a=1\) on \(W\) for the further axioms \(f_a\). Write each \(g_a\) as a combination of normal forms, of degree at most \(n/2\). Multiplying \(f_a\) by a normal form one variable at a time stays within degree \(n/2+w\), so \(P=\sum g_af_a\in C_{n/2+w}(\Gamma)\), and \(P-1\) vanishes on \(W\) with degree at most \(n/2+w\), hence lies in \(C_{n/2+w}(\Pi_n)\subseteq C_{n/2+w}(\Gamma)\) by part 1 of the proposition for the frame. 2. Standard monomials of \(C_D(\Gamma)\) are standard for \(C_D(\Pi_n)\), so extensions of \(z_A\) are among the nodes counted in part 3. For \(|A|=j-1\) with \(j\ge(2n+4)/5\), \(2(n-2j+2)-1<j\le(1+1/\Delta)j\). The bound \(w\) is not used in part 2, and \(1\notin C_D\), \(D\ge v^{1/2}\) are inherited from the theorem. \(\square\)

Reading. A contradiction over the frame meets the engine's requirement if its closure is proper at a cutoff \(D\ge2n/5+\lceil v^{1/3}\rceil+\Delta+1\), and none can be proper at or beyond \(n/2+w\). The plain cube on the same \(n\) leaves needs \(n/2-o(n)\) with only the general ceiling \(n+1\). The comparison is not favourable on its face: degree in the frame's variables is the number of dyadic blocks, so polynomials of degree \(0.4n\) include every \(y_T\) with at most \(0.4n\) blocks, and the expected number of blocks is \(0.36n\); the cutoff exceeds the mean by a linear margin, whereas on the cube the cutoff \(n/2-o(n)\) sits at the mean. The frame changes where the bulk sits, not the fact that the engine needs a barrier at or beyond it. A kernel's top standard monomial must here be an antichain of about \(0.4n\) non-sibling nodes all of whose sub-antichains stay irreducible.

What would decide it. A contradiction \(F\) on the leaves, of bounded width in frame variables, with no identity \(1=\sum g_af_a\) on \(W\) with multipliers \(g_a\) of frame degree at most \(0.4n-w\), and no dynamic shortcut. The static part asks for an odd-mass function on the cube orthogonal to every \(y_T f_a\) with few blocks. Since monomials of frame degree at most \(j\) include all leaf monomials of ordinary degree at most \(j\), and an axiom's leaf degree is at least its reduced frame degree, the static requirement is at least as strong as on the plain cube at cutoff \(0.4n\). No candidate is proposed in this entry.

Specification decision. No change. The frame shows that a clause admitting product-defined variables without counting them would be wrong as stated: such variables are counted by the extension condition through the cutoff \(2n/5\) of the leaves, not ignored, and the ceiling drops to \(n/2\) at the same time. A frame-specific clause, cutoff \(D\ge2n/5+o(n)\) for systems containing \(\Pi_n\), is justified by the corollary but is not adopted, since it has no witness with a proper closure there; under the rule in Where we stand a witness of the weakened specification would be needed and none is known.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer found no mathematical error and required corrections that are applied: the expectation is a finite sum and no concentration is claimed; the top degree is qualified by \(D\ge n/2\); the uniqueness and standardness steps are completed; the corollary's last step cites the frame's closure; the comparison with the cube now says the cutoff exceeds the mean here and sits at it there; the static requirement is stated in frame degree of multipliers. The reviewer's excerpt truncated the definition of the extension count; it is the number of variables \(x\) with \(x\,x_S\) standard, as assumed. Unused: the bound \(w\) and the slack \(1+1/\Delta\) in part 2 of the corollary; characteristic two in the proposition beyond signs. Dependencies reread in full: the forced extension entry and the thin-kernel review. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. No queue item is developed; the entry carries out the test named by the preceding entry.

Sub-ideas

  • Choose a contradiction over the product-tree frame and decide properness at \(0.4n\): start with symmetric conditions on the leaves and with two incompatible tree orders, and compute the static unit test at small heights only as a control for a stated general claim.
  • State and prove the general form suggested by the frame: the engine needs a cutoff beyond the degree at which level sizes of every down-closed subfamily stop growing; compare with the median degree of the standard monomials for an arbitrary frame.
  • Repeat the frame computation for trees of larger arity and for sums in place of products, to see whether the ratio of cutoff to ceiling, four fifths here, can be lowered.

Process assessment. This is the first explicit structure tested since the review, and it sharpens the reformulations into one number, the ratio of the engine's cutoff to the frame's ceiling. On the cube that ratio is one half of the trivial ceiling; here it is four fifths.
